20:T1809,Part of the corpus PII scrub pipeline — extends it to audio. Depends on `[pii] Transcript fragments with time anchors` (anchors + the audioUrl GC fix).

## Problem

Text scrubbing leaves PII audible in stored recordings (voice sessions, meetings). Needed: word-timestamp-aligned muting/bleeping that preserves duration (so every transcript anchor stays valid), a redacted variant stored as a second content-addressed object — original for OWNER/ADMIN, redacted for everyone else, composing with the permissioning epic — and a re-transcribe-verify loop proving the PII is actually inaudible.

## Architecture

- **Span production:** timed ASR per-word `{text, startMs, endMs}` via `eliza_inference_asr_transcribe_timed` (ABI v12 — `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/ffi-bindings.ts:395/918/1515/2193`, `timedAsrSupported()` gate; real-audio contract test `asr-timed.real.test.ts`). Text-PII verdicts from the LLM-pass over anchored transcript fragments merge onto word spans → `[{startMs, endMs}]` with padding. Pseudonym labels for spans come from the corpus map (`[pii] Context-retrieval pass`) so audio and text redaction agree on identity.
- **Mute op (empirically verified on ffmpeg 8.1.1):** `ffmpeg -i in -af "volume=0:enable='between(t,S1,E1)+between(t,S2,E2)+...'" -c:a <codec> out` — spans compose by summing `between()` terms. Bleep variant: `-f lavfi -i "sine=f=1000"` + `filter_complex` `amix duration=first`. Measured: WAV → exact duration, −91 dB true silence in span; OGG/opus → exact; M4A/AAC → +1 trailing encoder frame — assert duration with ±(1024/sampleRate)s tolerance or normalize through WAV. Sample count within the stream never changes, so span coordinates remain valid in the redacted variant.
- **Runtime capability:** ffmpeg is desktop/server-only (`packages/agent/src/runtime/core-plugins.ts:168`, `packages/core/src/runtime-env.ts:410` — iOS/Android/workers have none); probe like `whichBin('ffmpeg')` in `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/mic-source.ts`. The voice pipeline's native format is 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV (`ASR_SAMPLE_RATE`), so pure-TS PCM sample zeroing covers WAV with no ffmpeg at all; ffmpeg is the lane for lossy formats. Hosted option: a `media-redact` Railway sibling of `packages/cloud/services/voice-whisper-stt` (same Dockerfile/railway.toml/live-test pattern) — workerd cannot run ffmpeg, cloud-api may only orchestrate.
- **Storage (#8876-clean):** redacted bytes → `persistMediaBytes` (`packages/agent/src/api/media-store.ts:291`) → new sha256 object at `${STATE_DIR}/media/<sha256'>.<ext>`, served at `/api/media/<sha256'>.<ext>`. No new store, no files table, no fileId. Additive optional `Media` field only (sanctioned by the additive-widening block at `packages/core/src/types/primitives.ts:243-249`), e.g. `redactedOf?: string` (source sha) or `variant?: "redacted"`.
- **Permissioning (composes with the epic):** media bytes are served pre-auth — the sha256 is the capability — so enforcement lives at REFERENCE DISTRIBUTION, not the serve path: the transcript/document DTO carries the ORIGINAL sha URL only for `Role.OWNER`/`ADMIN` (`packages/core/src/types/environment.ts:43-51`; `packages/agent/src/api/boundary-role-resolver.ts`), the redacted sha for everyone else; the original hash must never enter non-privileged message records/context. GC: `gcUnreferencedMedia` (`media-store.ts:503`) keeps each variant alive only while referenced.
- **Re-transcribe-verify loop:** redacted bytes → `runtime.useModel(ModelType.TRANSCRIPTION, {audio, transcriptionPurpose: "interim"})` (`TranscriptionParams`, `packages/core/src/types/model.ts:940-952`; local handler = fused eliza-1-asr; `AsrUnavailableError` ⇒ the verify step FAILS, never a vacuous pass) → assert (a) every PII token ABSENT — exact + normalized fuzzy match, NOT transcript equality (Whisper-family models hallucinate filler over silence), and (b) sentinel non-PII words still PRESENT (over-mute guard). Cloud variant: POST the redacted file to voice-whisper-stt `/v1/audio/transcriptions`.
- Text-side precedent: trajectory redaction (`packages/agent/src/runtime/trajectory-internals.ts:1304` `redactTrajectoryParams`).

## Acceptance criteria

- E2E on real audio: fixture WAV (freeman.wav or a purpose-recorded fixture with planted PII) → spans → mute AND bleep variants across wav/ogg/m4a; per-codec duration assertions; `volumedetect` proves ≤ −85 dB in muted windows.
- **Redacted-audio artifact opened and LISTENED to by a human** — attach the redacted audio inline in the PR (MP4) with a note of what was heard. Hard evidence gate.
- Re-transcribe-verify test in the `*.real.test.ts` lane (skipped-never-faked when `ELIZA_INFERENCE_LIBRARY`/`ELIZA_ASR_BUNDLE` absent): PII absent, sentinels present; a deliberately broken run (one span omitted) FAILS the verify.
- Role test: OWNER DTO carries the original URL; USER/GUEST DTO carries only the redacted URL; a scan proves the original sha never appears in non-privileged room records.
- GC test: both variants referenced → both survive; original dereferenced (retention state flipped) → original collected, redacted survives.
- Idempotency: same input sha + same spans + same ruleset version ⇒ identical output sha; the pipeline done-marker makes re-runs no-ops.
- Constrained-runtime behavior: without ffmpeg, WAV redaction still works (pure-TS zeroing) and lossy-format redaction fails observably (typed error via `runtime.reportError`), never silently skipped.

## Out of scope

Video/image redaction; live/streaming redaction; any files/refcount table (#8876); serve-path auth changes (the capability model stands); forced-alignment ASR upgrades (char-weighted timing is the documented baseline).

## Pipeline integration

Extends the corpus pipeline to multimodal: LLM-pass verdicts (with corpus-consistent pseudonym labels from the context pass) become timestamp spans via the transcript-anchor issue; execution rides `[pii] Async scrub job rails` and the shared `pii:<sha256>:v<ruleset>` idempotency layer; the variant swap is the audio analog of the text write-back stage.

`app-staging.elizacloud.ai` is stuck on **"initializing agent"** for every new agent. Root cause: **every agent-create call to the staging cloud-api returns HTTP 500 `{"code":"internal_error"}`**. The UI provisions the agent, then polls the per-agent proxy passthrough (`GET /api/conversations`) which never serves (the agent was never created), so `runCloudManagedWarmup()` spins on `initializing-agent` until the warmup deadline.

The 500 is an **unhandled DB/infrastructure error** inside the create handler, forced to the generic `internal_error` envelope by `isInfrastructureError()` in `cloud-worker-errors.ts` (so the real SQLSTATE/SQL message is swallowed to avoid leaking raw SQL).

## Reproduction (staging, authenticated session)
```

POST /api/v1/eliza/agents {"agentName":"x","autoProvision":true,"dockerImage":"ghcr.io/elizaos/eliza-agent:latest"} → 500 internal_error (t≈7.6s)
```
Both shared and dedicated create paths 500 → it's the create **write**, not provisioning/worker-health.

## Reads are healthy — this is write/transaction-specific
```

GET /api/v1/credits/balance → 200 {"balance":…} (t≈1.3s)
GET /api/health             → 200 environment:staging
```
- Bogus `dockerImage` → **403 agent_image_not_allowed** (handler reaches deep into `createAgent`/`assertAgentImageAllowed`; the write AFTER the allowlist gate is what fails).
- `getReadConnection()` and `getWriteConnection()` both resolve the **same** `getPrimaryDatabaseUrl()`/Hyperdrive binding, so this is NOT a code-level read/write DB split. The difference: create runs a **multi-statement interactive `dbWrite.transaction`** with a Postgres advisory lock + `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` + INSERT (`eliza-sandbox.ts` `createAgent`), while a passing read is a single pooled query.

Part of the LifeOps MVP program — see packages/docs/ongoing-development/mvp/MVP.md (workstream 7).28:T580,Found during review of #16977.

Pool containers are provisioned under the sentinel `WARM_POOL_ORG_ID`, so `prepareManagedElizaBaseEnvironment` mints their `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY` (via `apiKeysService.createForAgent`) for the POOL org/user. `claimWarmContainer` transfers the DB row to the claiming user's org, and #16977 transfers the boot-coupled inbound auth keys — but the RUNNING container's outbound cloud identity (`ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY` in its process env) still belongs to the pool org until the next container restart re-materializes env from the row.

Consequences in the window between claim and first restart:
- cloud-API usage from the container (inference routing, usage tracking) attributes to the pool org, not the claiming org — billing/limits skew;
- revoking the claiming org's keys does not cut the container's cloud access, and vice versa.

Possible directions: mint the agent API key at claim time and include it in the post-claim push path (needs a container-side route to swap `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY` live), or rotate via a fast restart out-of-band after claim, or re-attribute pool-key usage rows at claim time. Needs design — the claim path's latency budget is the whole point of the warm pool.

2a:T8c1,## Problem

`computeEffectiveMaxTokens` currently applies:

`Math.max(request.max_tokens, 4096)`

to every model classified as using reasoning tokens. Both pass-through and SDK paths send that raised value upstream.

A client requesting `max_tokens:512` therefore authorizes an upstream ceiling of 4096 without any response field or header indicating that the request was changed.

The controlled Gemma/GLM latency run discovered this because direct requests used 512 while the gateway silently sent 4096, invalidating the original comparison.

## Why this is delicate

The floor was intentionally introduced by #8189/#8486 to prevent reasoning models from consuming a low budget entirely in hidden reasoning and returning an empty but billed answer. It must not simply be deleted.

Nevertheless, silently increasing an explicit caller ceiling is an API-contract and money-integrity problem: it can permit more generation, reservation, and spend than the caller requested.

## Required decision

Choose and document one safe contract:

1. Preserve an explicit caller cap; only apply a default floor when the field is absent.
2. Reject a reasoning-enabled request whose cap is too small with a clear 4xx.
3. Permit a low cap when reasoning is explicitly disabled.
4. Introduce explicit answer-vs-reasoning budget semantics.

Whichever contract is selected, expose requested and effective values in bounded telemetry and ensure billing admission uses the same effective value sent upstream.

## Acceptance

- An explicit output ceiling is never silently increased.
- Low-budget reasoning requests cannot regress to misleading `finish_reason:"stop"` with empty billed content.
- GLM-4.7 with `reasoning_effort:"none"` can use a genuinely small budget.
- Streaming and non-streaming routes behave consistently.
- Reservations and final billing are tested against the exact provider-facing budget.
- The benchmark harness records both requested and effective budgets.
- Compatibility behavior is documented.

## References

- Original broad floor: #8189
- Launch-model detection extension: #8486
- Equivalent `/v1/messages` history: #12864 / #12865
- Cerebras Chat Completions:
  https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/api-reference/chat-completions
2b:T939,## Problem

`zai-glm-4.7` — the default `TEXT_LARGE` model on Cerebras since #16261 — is a hybrid reasoning model (streams a separate `reasoning` delta channel), but `isReasoningModel()` in `plugins/plugin-openai/models/text.ts` does not match it. Two consequences on a local Cerebras runtime (`ELIZA_PROVIDER=cerebras`, `OPENAI_LARGE_MODEL=zai-glm-4.7`):

1. The Cerebras-mode `reasoning_effort: "low"` default (added for exactly this failure on `gpt-oss-120b`) never applies to GLM, so its reasoning runs unbounded.
2. `providerOptions.eliza.thinking = "off"` — set by core's planner loop (`packages/core/src/runtime/planner-loop.ts:1549`), Stage-1 formatting calls (`packages/core/src/services/message.ts:8770`), and the app-model-tester — is silently ignored by plugin-openai, while plugin-elizacloud maps it to each Cerebras model's suppression value (`resolveCerebrasThinkingOffReasoningEffort`, `plugins/plugin-elizacloud/src/models/text.ts:366`).

With a capped `max_tokens` the model spends the entire budget on hidden reasoning and returns **empty visible content** with `finish_reason: "length"`.

## Reproduction (live Cerebras, wire-captured via a logging proxy)

`POST /api/model-tester/run {"test":"text-large"}` on a default local Cerebras setup, 8 runs. Every request went out as `{"model":"zai-glm-4.7","max_tokens":160}` with **no** `reasoning_effort`:

```
4x  finish_reason:"length"  reasoning_tokens:160/160  → "TEXT_LARGE returned empty text"
4x  finish_reason:"stop"    reasoning_tokens:62–157   → "pong"
```

~50% failure, purely dependent on how long GLM happens to reason. Direct curl confirms the mechanism: `reasoning_effort:"low"` bounds reasoning (~20–30 tokens), and `reasoning_effort:"none"` (accepted by gemma/GLM, rejected by gpt-oss) eliminates it entirely (`reasoning_tokens: 0`).

## Fix

PR incoming, mirroring plugin-elizacloud's settled semantics:

- add the GLM family to `isReasoningModel()` so the Cerebras `"low"` default applies;
- honor `eliza.thinking === "off"` in Cerebras mode by mapping it per model: `"none"` for gemma/GLM, `"low"` for gpt-oss; explicit caller `providerOptions.openai.reasoningEffort` still wins.

After the fix (same wire capture): 10/10 probes return content, `finish_reason:"stop"`, `reasoning_tokens: 0`.

`packages/core/src/features/documents/service.ts` writes the parent DOCUMENT row (`createMemory(memoryWithScope, DOCUMENTS_TABLE)`) **before** `processFragmentsSynchronously`, and the `addDocument` catch only logs and rethrows — there is no `deleteMemory` compensation. So while **validation-time** failures now persist nothing (fixed by #16002's pre-write `validatePreChunkedFragments` hoist), an **embed-time** failure (model down, embedding dimension mismatch) still leaves an orphaned zero-fragment document row in the index: visible in document lists, unmatchable in fragment search.

The failure is at least observable now (typed throw + `runtime.reportError` at the mirrors), but the orphan row remains.

**Fix options:** compensating `deleteMemory` of the parent row in the failure path of `addDocument` (preferred — restores all-or-nothing at the document level), or a reconciliation sweep that removes zero-fragment DOCUMENT rows older than a grace window.

## 1. Discord login failure at boot is terminal — no retry

A transient network blip at exactly the wrong moment produced:

```
Registered Discord message connector for account default
Warn  Failed to login to Discord account default: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly.
```

…and the bot then ran for **19 minutes fully deaf** — process `active`, task scheduler humming, zero inbound processing — until a manual restart. discord.js reconnects fine once a gateway session exists; the gap is the **initial** `login()` rejection, which is never retried. A connector whose transport failed to establish should retry with backoff (and keep retrying), not settle into a permanently-connected-looking corpse. The memory-watchdog precedent (#10197) applies: surface + self-heal via the existing restart/retry seams.

## 2. Inbound message ~2.5 min after boot silently dropped — zero trace

After the recovery restart (`Discord client ready for account default` at 23:51:09):

- **23:53:46** — a mention arrives (`use a coding agent to write countdown.py …`). **No trace whatsoever**: no `Processing message`, no triage decision, no staleness tag, nothing. The message is visible in channel history; the bot never saw it or dropped it pre-log.
- **00:00:22** — an identical-format mention (`what is 3 plus 4`) processes instantly and answers.
- Re-sending the identical countdown prompt later: routed `coding → elizaos`, completed clean in 37s.

So there is a window after `ready` (room/world sync? backfill?) where a live inbound message can be dropped **with no log line at any level**. Whatever the gating condition is, a dropped inbound must at least log at Warn with the reason — silent drops are indistinguishable from user error.

## Current path

The chat handler first calls resolveInferenceAuthContext. For an API key it:

1. reads the inference auth context from the shared cache;
2. on a hit, returns the fully authorized user/org/key context;
3. on a miss, runs requireAuthOrApiKeyWithOrg;
4. checks moderation authoritatively; and
5. writes the positive context back to cache.

Worker auto-cache configuration prefers the bound CACHE_KV namespace. Therefore the current evidence proves a cache-hit versus authoritative-path split, but does not yet identify whether the 3.2 seconds are KV read/miss behavior, database auth/org queries, moderation, the cache write, or cold dependency/connection setup. #16079 must name those boundaries before optimizing.

Relevant code:
- packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/inference-auth-context.ts
- packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/inference-auth-cache.ts
- packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/cache/client.ts
- packages/cloud/api/v1/chat/completions/route.ts

## Required work

- Add privacy-safe correlated timings for credential extraction, cache availability, KV hit/miss/invalid, authoritative key lookup, user/org lookup, moderation, and cache write.
- Record only bounded source/result enums and timings; never log presented keys, hashes, auth headers, prompts, or user-controlled identifiers.
- Reproduce cache hits and controlled cache misses in staging across fresh Worker versions/placements.
- Optimize the proven slow boundary. Candidates include a single authoritative join, parallel independent checks, Hyperdrive/connection placement, or a strongly consistent edge auth primitive. Choose from evidence.
- Preserve fail-closed invalid/revoked/inactive/suspended behavior and exact 401/403 taxonomy. Do not add an un-invalidated positive L1 cache or relax revocation to reduce latency.

## Acceptance

- One trace distinguishes cache hit, cache miss, cache unavailable, and every authoritative sub-hop.
- At least 30 fresh-version/cache-hit probes and 10 controlled staging cache-miss probes are retained with exact deployed SHA.
- Cache-hit auth p95 stays below 50 ms and has no requests above 250 ms.
- Controlled authoritative auth has no multi-second tail and improves by at least 50% at p90 versus the current evidence.
- API-key revoke/update/delete, user/org deactivate, moderation suspension, malformed cache entries, and cache outage retain existing fail-closed semantics and tests.

3f:T17d0,## Summary

The Cloud chat gateway still adds seconds before a Cerebras request despite the provider itself being fast. A paired staging benchmark now isolates the dominant regression: chat crosses **three Railway-TCP Redis rate-limit gates** before provider forwarding. After 30 seconds idle, the two Hono middleware gates alone add **2.45–3.11s** outside the route timer, and the handler's org gate contributes to another **0.51–0.97s** phase. Direct Cerebras remains **0.09–0.37s**.

This is not reasoning-effort overhead and it is not slow Cerebras generation. The actual gateway-to-Cerebras response-header phase was **0.09–0.33s** in every post-idle case.

### Independent live-tail confirmation on current staging

On commit `b2e36d3`, privacy-safe unauthenticated chat probes reproduced both modes without ever calling a model provider:

- successful Railway Redis check: 556–589ms wall
- SocketRedis timeout: 2.378s, 3.250s, and 3.459s wall
- exact log: `SocketRedis operation timed out after 1000ms`
- degraded response policy: `redis-unavailable` (the limiter fell open)

Across 679 successful Worker requests in the prior 30 minutes, p95 wall time was 3.40s and p99 was 8.49s. `/api/health`, which bypasses the lazy full-app import, stayed at 0–1ms; cold chat also pays initialization for the monolithic 580-route app.

## Code-level cause

Every chat call currently stacks:

1. `bootstrap-app.ts`: global Hono IP limiter (600/min), before the chat route timer.
2. `v1/chat/completions/route.ts`: Hono API-key limiter (200/min), also before the timer.
3. `handleChatCompletionsPOST`: per-org tier limiter (60/120/300 per minute).

All three use `REDIS_URL` in staging/production. `redis-factory.ts` resolves that to `SocketRedis` over `cloudflare:sockets`, opening request-scoped TCP/TLS connections to Railway. The committed Wrangler comments simultaneously state that raw external Redis from Workers is unreliable and can hang under load. `SocketRedis` has a 1,000ms operation timeout, so the measured two outer stalls plus one inner stall match the three connection/operation failure windows. Its error cleanup awaits an unbounded `close()` sequence, so the documented 1s ceiling is not actually a wall-clock ceiling; that is consistent with 3–4.66s outside-route outliers.

The existing `X-Eliza-Preforward-Ms` header starts inside `handleChatCompletionsPOST`, so it cannot see the largest two gates and currently labels provider-header wait as `total`. This is tracked more broadly in #16079.

## Required fix

- Replace the protective global and chat route Redis gates with Cloudflare's native Rate Limiting binding. It is machine-local/non-network-blocking and designed for protective limits.
- Keep the organization-tier limit on a globally strong backend. Cloudflare's native binding is location-local and eventually consistent, so silently substituting it would weaken the purchased org quota. Batch its lease reconciliation and use one request-scoped connection or a strong Cloudflare primitive such as a Durable Object.
- Preserve explicit 429 behavior and observable policy headers/logs. Missing/misconfigured production bindings must fail visibly, not silently disable protection.
- Bound SocketRedis teardown so an operation timeout remains a real wall-clock ceiling for non-chat consumers.
- Extend correlated telemetry across global limiter, route limiter, auth, org tier lookup/limit, pool selection, balance gate/reservation, provider fetch-to-headers, first byte/token, stream completion, and deferred settlement.
- Keep production untouched until staging proves the change.

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit/integration tests cover allow, deny, binding failure/missing binding, batched lease reconciliation, and no duplicate counter increments.
- Wrangler dry-run and generated binding types pass for staging and production config.
- A real staging paired run repeats the same five Cerebras cases with at least 30 warm pairs/case plus 30-second post-idle probes, paced below limits.
- Post-idle paired excess outside the route timer (`gateway headers - route total - matched direct headers`) has p90 below 100ms, and no Redis TCP timeout appears in the two protective chat ingress limiters.
- Gateway provider-to-headers remains within 2x direct after subtracting deliberate auth/billing work; all remaining deltas are named by truthful telemetry.
- Billing reservations/deferred settlement, auth failures, 402s, and 429s retain their existing correctness semantics.

42:T1350,## Problem

#16207 intentionally changed `NotificationService.start()` to fail when persisted notification state cannot be read instead of treating an unreadable durable inbox as a healthy empty inbox (the acceptance criterion in #16206).

That fail-closed contract is currently lost at the next boundary:

- `packages/agent/src/api/notification-routes.ts` returns HTTP 200 with `{ notifications: [], unreadCount: 0 }` for `GET /api/notifications` whenever `runtime.getService(ServiceType.NOTIFICATION)` is absent.
- `plugins/plugin-capacitor-bridge/src/android/dispatch.ts` has the same fallback for the Android UDS route.
- Neither route distinguishes an intentionally disabled/unregistered service from `pending`, `registering`, or `failed` service state. After a cache-read failure, `AgentRuntime._runServiceStart()` marks the service `failed` and leaves no instance, so both routes convert the failure back into a healthy empty inbox.
- `packages/ui/src/state/notifications/notification-store.ts` hydrates once. On a transport/5xx failure it logs, sets `hydrated: true`, preserves the live WebSocket subscription, but schedules no HTTP hydration retry. A transient startup race or recovered persistence layer can therefore leave persisted history absent for the whole UI session.
- The HTTP route comment says the UI “degrades gracefully and retries,” but no such retry currently exists.

This is a fail-closed integration/recovery gap. It is **not** the packaged App Live native-notification failure: that test injects a mock WebSocket `agent_event`, does not start core `NotificationService`, and the observed failing run predates #16207.

## Required behavior

1. Preserve #16207's fail-closed persistence semantics. Do not restore the blanket `hydrate()` catch that turns an unreadable inbox into empty state.
2. Give notification routes enough runtime lifecycle information to distinguish:
   - intentionally disabled/unregistered notification support;
   - `pending` / `registering` startup;
   - `failed` startup;
   - a registered service instance.
3. For `pending` / `registering`, return a typed retryable 503 response (for example `NOTIFICATION_SERVICE_NOT_READY`) and a bounded `Retry-After` value instead of HTTP 200 empty.
4. For `failed`, return a typed 503 response (for example `NOTIFICATION_SERVICE_FAILED`) without leaking adapter/secrets/internal error details. Never represent failed persistence as an empty successful inbox.
5. Define the intentional disabled/headless contract explicitly. If that case remains HTTP 200 empty, it must be positively identified rather than inferred from a missing service instance.
6. Add bounded, jittered/background UI hydrate retry that:
   - honors `Retry-After` when present;
   - does not clear already received notifications;
   - keeps the live WebSocket subscription active;
   - avoids duplicate subscriptions/delivery;
   - stops after a documented cap and exposes/logs the terminal hydrate error rather than silently reading as healthy empty.
7. Add explicit, single-flight service recovery/backoff for transient notification hydration failures. Recovery may live at the runtime service boundary or in a dedicated route/service coordinator, but requests must not create a retry stampede. A recovered cache adapter must be able to rehydrate persisted history without restarting the entire agent.
8. Apply equivalent semantics to the Android UDS notification route.
9. Emit enough structured diagnostics/telemetry to distinguish disabled, not-ready, failed, retrying, recovered, and terminal-retry-exhausted states.

## Tests

- `packages/core/src/services/notification.test.ts`
  - unreadable cache still fails startup;
  - a transient cache-read failure can recover through the chosen explicit recovery path;
  - concurrent recovery requests are single-flight / bounded.
- `packages/agent/src/api/notification-routes.test.ts`
  - pending/registering GET is typed 503 + `Retry-After`, not 200 empty;
  - failed GET is typed 503, not 200 empty;
  - intentionally disabled/unregistered behavior is explicit;
  - registered service returns persisted rows.
- `packages/ui/src/state/notifications/notification-store.test.ts` (or the canonical store test file)
  - bounded retry and `Retry-After` handling with fake timers;
  - state received over WS is preserved while HTTP hydrate retries;
  - successful recovery merges/sets persisted history without duplicate delivery;
  - terminal exhaustion is observable and does not create an infinite timer/subscription loop.
- `plugins/plugin-capacitor-bridge/src/android/dispatch.test.ts`
  - lifecycle-state response parity with the HTTP route;
  - recovered service serves persisted rows.

## Non-goals

- Do not conflate this with the separate App Live packaged native-notification test failure.
- Do not mask cache/adapter failures as empty state.
- Do not retry every incoming request independently.

- Split the Anthropic billing/preflight work from UI flow repairs if ownership differs.45:Tc11,Sibling to #16021 (which fixed the *create*-path orphan). The **edit** path (`DocumentService.updateDocument`) has a strictly worse, non-atomic failure mode: an embed-time failure during re-fragmentation **destroys the document's existing, working fragments** and leaves the parent row showing the new content with **zero fragments** — data loss on edit, not just an orphan on create.

## Root cause

`packages/core/src/features/documents/service.ts` `updateDocument` performs a destructive re-fragmentation in this order:

1. `runtime.updateMemory(...)` — overwrites the parent `DOCUMENT` row with the **new** content/metadata.
2. Deletes **every existing fragment** for the document (`deleteMemory` in a loop over `relatedFragments`).
3. `splitAndCreateFragments(...)` then `processDocumentFragmentsBatched(fragments, { continueOnError: false })` — re-embeds and persists the new fragments.

Step 3 embeds via `addEmbeddingToMemory → useModel(TEXT_EMBEDDING)`. When the embedding backend is unavailable or returns a dimension/shape mismatch — the exact failure class #16021 addressed for the create path — `processDocumentFragmentsBatched` with `continueOnError: false` **throws**. But by then:

- the old (working) fragments are already **deleted**, and
- the parent row already holds the **new** text.

Result: the document is now **searchable-empty** (parent visible in lists, unmatchable in fragment/vector/BM25 search) **and the previously-working fragments are permanently gone**. The caller (`documents` action `handleEdit`, and `plugin-documents` PATCH route) gets a thrown error, but the store is already corrupted — there is no compensation and no snapshot to restore.

## Why #16021's fix does not cover this

#16021 / PR #16103 add all-or-nothing compensation to the **create** path (`addDocument`/`processDocument`): on embed failure the freshly-written parent row is rolled back. `updateDocument` is a separate method with a *mutating* sequence (overwrite parent + delete old fragments **before** the new embeds), so it needs a different, snapshot-based repair, not a parent-row delete.

## Acceptance

- An embed-time (or fragment-persist) failure during `updateDocument` must **not** leave the document with fewer fragments than it had before, and must **not** silently swap in the new content while dropping all fragments.
- Preferred: stage the new fragments first (embed + validate before any destructive delete/overwrite), and only swap parent content + delete-old + insert-new once the new fragments are known-good; on failure, the pre-edit state is preserved and a typed `ElizaError` propagates. (A snapshot/restore of the old fragments + parent content is an acceptable alternative.)
- Surface the failure via `runtime.reportError("DocumentService.updateDocument", …)` consistent with #16021.
- Add fails-before/passes-after coverage: embed-down during re-fragmentation, fragment-persist throw, and a healthy edit (must still re-fragment). Prove old fragments survive on failure.

Found during post-#16021 review of the documents mutation surface.
46:T4fd,Child of #16064 (LP3 device-integration batch, root-caused live on a Light Phone III).

## Bug

Every streamed assistant voice reply is spoken **twice**. A streaming reply is first announced to `queueAssistantSpeech` under the provisional client id (`temp-resp-*` from `useChatSend`), then re-announced with identical (or extended) text under its persisted server id.

In `packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts`, `queueAssistantSpeech` treats the id flip as a brand-new assistant message and resets `assistantSpeechRef` — including `queuedSpeakablePrefix` — so the whole already-spoken reply is re-queued and played again. Heard live as the agent repeating every answer a beat later.

## Fix

When the promoted message's speakable text continues (or is a prefix of) what the previous state already queued, carry `queuedSpeakablePrefix` and `finalQueued` across the id change instead of resetting. Genuinely new messages (different text) still reset as before.

## Repro (unit)

1. `queueAssistantSpeech("temp-resp-123", text, true)` → speaks once.
2. `queueAssistantSpeech("srv-msg-456", text, true)` → **before fix**: speaks the whole reply again; **after fix**: no-op.
3. Extended-final variant: only the unspoken remainder is queued.

4b:Tea0,### Problem

`dryRun`/`mode:"prepare"` means two different things depending on which layer of `plugin-wallet` you hit, and **neither actually simulates a transaction**:

1. **`WalletBackendService.routeWalletAction`** (`services/wallet-backend-service.ts:154-205`): when `params.dryRun || params.mode === "prepare"`, it returns a **hardcoded object literal** echoing the input params — `handler.execute()` is never called. No network request happens at all. (Only `subaction:"bridge"` calls `execute()` in prepare mode — every other subaction, including `swap`, short-circuits.)
2. **`SolanaService.swap({dryRun:true})`** (`chains/solana/service.ts:644-717`): this one *does* call `buildJupiterSwapTransaction` unconditionally at `:661` — a real `GET quote-api.jup.ag/v6/quote` + `POST /v6/swap`, returning a real serialized `swapTransaction`. But then the `if (dryRun)` branch at `:669` **discards that built transaction** and returns `{txid:null, dryRun:true, ...}` without ever deserializing, signing, or simulating it.
3. **pump.fun** (`chains/registry.ts:518-616`, `executePumpFunBuy`) has **no dry-run branch at all** — it always POSTs to PumpPortal `trade-local`, deserializes the response into a `VersionedTransaction`, signs, and sends.
4. There is **no `connection.simulateTransaction` call anywhere on the swap/transfer/pump.fun path.** The only `simulateTransaction` usage in the whole plugin is inside `dex/orca/utils/sendTransaction.ts` and the Meteora equivalent, as a pre-send compute-budget step *inside* a function that then sends — not reachable as a standalone check.

Net effect: an agent integrating `plugin-wallet` for autonomous/semi-autonomous trading has **no way to validate that a real trade will succeed** — that a route exists right now, what the price impact and slippage are, that the transaction actually builds, and that it fits the compute budget — before the very first real submission. The expensive, informative work (steps 1-2 above: quoting Jupiter, building the tx) already happens on the `SolanaService.swap` dry-run path and is thrown away one line later.

Verified against `develop @ 184a4cc85072165a2cd911cb65c50d6a5c409326`.

### Proposal

Add a third, **strictly additive** mode alongside today's `prepare`/`execute` (or `dryRun: true|false`): `mode: "simulate"`.

- Build the transaction exactly as the live path does today (real quote, real `swapTransaction`/pump.fun `trade-local` response, real deserialize).
- Instead of signing + `connection.sendTransaction(...)`, call `connection.simulateTransaction(tx, { sigVerify: false, replaceRecentBlockhash: true })` — this runs against an **unsigned** transaction, so `simulate` mode needs only a public key, never a private key.
- Return the simulation result instead of a `txid`: expected output amount, price-impact/slippage from the quote, the route plan, `unitsConsumed` from the simulation, and `err`/logs when it would revert.
- `prepare` (today's offline echo) and `execute` (today's real send) are **completely unchanged** — this is a new opt-in branch, not a replacement, so it can't break any existing consumer of `routeWalletAction`/`SolanaService.swap`.

### Why this matters beyond one integration

Any elizaOS agent doing autonomous fund movement hits the same gap: "dry run" today either does nothing (offline echo) or does real work and throws it away. A real simulate mode is the only way to validate a trade end-to-end — real liquidity, real route, real compute cost — with zero funds at risk (no private key required). I'm happy to contribute a PR for the Solana side (Jupiter swap + pump.fun) if that's useful; I already have a working mirror of this exact logic in our integration and can generalize it.

4d:T1136,## Summary

Migrate Eliza's native typechecking from the retired `@typescript/native-preview` / `tsgo` path to stable TypeScript 7, while retaining TypeScript 6 only for compiler-API consumers that cannot migrate until the TypeScript 7 API is available.

TypeScript 7.0.2 became stable on 2026-07-08. Microsoft now publishes the native compiler as `typescript` with the `tsc` executable and recommends `@typescript/typescript6` for side-by-side API compatibility.

## Current state

- Root declares `@typescript/native-preview: ^7.0.0-dev.20260421.2` and `typescript: ^6.0.3`.
- The lock resolves native preview `7.0.0-dev.20260628.1` and TypeScript `6.0.3`.
- About 223 of 256 effective workspace typechecks (~87%) already use native `tsgo`, including Cloud API, routing, shared, SDK, and plugin-elizacloud.
- About 32 effective checks remain on legacy `tsc`; several are deliberate compatibility exceptions, while others are nested workspaces not currently audited.
- At least 26 repository consumers import or require the TypeScript 6 compiler API. A blind root `typescript` bump would break AST tooling, tenant-scope checks, runtime transpilation fallbacks, declaration workflows, and peer dependencies.
- Stable TypeScript 7 exposes `tsc`, not `tsgo`, so removing native-preview without migrating scripts would break more than 220 workspace commands.

## Why

- Use the supported stable compiler instead of a June preview build.
- Receive stable TypeScript 7 fixes, LSP behavior, and release support.
- Preserve the native compiler's material local/CI speedup. Microsoft reports typical 8–12x full-build improvements and lower aggregate memory versus TypeScript 6.
- Make compiler selection explicit and reproducible instead of relying on an indefinitely retained preview package.

This does **not** improve application, Worker, Cerebras, or gateway runtime latency; it improves compiler, CI, and editor feedback time.

## Safe migration shape

1. Preserve the TypeScript 6 API under the official compatibility package/alias, for example:

   ```json
   {
     "devDependencies": {
       "@typescript/native": "npm:typescript@^7.0.2",
       "typescript": "npm:@typescript/typescript6@^6.0.2"
     }
   }
   ```

2. Replace standard native-check commands from `tsgo` to the stable TypeScript 7 `tsc` binary, without redirecting API-dependent tooling away from the TypeScript 6 alias.
3. Inventory and migrate package-local TypeScript declarations in waves; the repo currently contains TS 5.x, TS 6.0.x, and root-hoisted consumers.
4. Audit TypeScript 7 hard errors/default changes (`baseUrl`, legacy module resolution, ES5/downlevel emit, `types`, `rootDir`, strict/module defaults, and JS/JSDoc differences).
5. Byte/API-compare declaration output for core packages and all dist-path consumers before changing emit commands.
6. Run Linux, macOS, and Windows validation for root typecheck/build/pack, Cloud Worker dry-runs, and editor/LSP behavior.
7. Benchmark warm/cold wall time and peak memory for root and Cloud typechecks. Tune `--checkers` and Turbo concurrency together; multiple native compilers already exhausted 16 GB CI runners in prior work.
8. Keep a documented TypeScript 6 rollback path until TypeScript 7.1's compiler API and peer ecosystem are validated.

## Related cleanup

- Fix the compiler-model audit to discover every declared workspace rather than only top-level packages and one nested level.
- Re-evaluate stale exceptions: personal-assistant now passes native checking, and plugin-streaming already emits with `--noCheck`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Stable TypeScript 7 is pinned and locked project-locally; no global compiler is required.
- [ ] All intended native typechecks use stable `tsc` and no scripts depend on the retired `tsgo` binary.
- [ ] TypeScript 6 API consumers resolve through an explicit compatibility alias/package.
- [ ] Full workspace discovery/audit passes with every exception documented.
- [ ] Root verify, full CI, Cloud tests/Worker dry-run, dist consumers, package/runtime export checks, and declaration comparisons pass.
- [ ] Before/after wall-time and peak-memory results are attached for representative local and CI runs.
- [ ] Editor setup and rollback guidance are documented.

## References

- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/
- https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go/blob/main/CHANGES.md

4e:T1240,## Goal

The chat overlay on iOS and Android should be a **native material surface** — real liquid glass (`UIGlassEffect`) on iOS 26+, the Material dynamic-palette panel on Android 12+ — wrapped via Capacitor, with everything piped between native and web, and web-rendered CSS glass as the fallback tier on web/desktop/older OS versions. Optimized for speed: the native tier replaces the WebView's per-frame `backdrop-filter: blur(30px)` on the dragged sheet (the single biggest GPU/battery cost per #9141) with an OS-composited material.

## What already exists (after the GlassBridge parity PR)

- `GlassBridge` Capacitor plugin on **both** platforms with an identical JS API (`attachGlass` / `updateRect` / `detachGlass` / `setGrouping` / `isAvailable`): iOS 26 `UIGlassEffect` (`packages/app-core/platforms/ios/App/App/GlassBridge.swift`), Android 12+ Material panel (`packages/app-core/platforms/android/.../GlassBridgePlugin.java`).
- The TS tier system: `packages/ui/src/glass/` — `useNativeGlass()` (`native` / `css-refraction` / `css-frosted`), `GlassSurface` (attach-on-mount, ResizeObserver rect sync, transparent element on the native tier), memoized availability probe, CSS fallback identical on every tier.
- The chat sheet's CSS glass (`ContinuousChatOverlay.tsx` — `blur(30px) saturate(1.4)` + rim + sheen on the inset sheet).

## The blocker: the wallpaper is web-rendered

The native material sits **under** the WebView and shows through only where the page is transparent all the way down. Today `AppBackground` (shader/image wallpaper) renders in the DOM — so behind the chat sheet there are always web pixels, and an under-WebView glass region would show the black window background instead of the wallpaper. This is why the sheet still uses the CSS tier.

## Architecture to land

1. **Native-hosted wallpaper (the enabling move).** Extend the bridge (or a sibling `WallpaperBridge`) with `setBackdrop({ imageUrl?, color? })`:
   - iOS: a `UIImageView`/solid layer inserted below the WebView; Android: an `ImageView`/drawable below the WebView.
   - Web: when the native tier is available and the active `BackgroundConfig` is an **image** background, `AppBackground` pipes the image to native (through the existing content-addressed media store URL) and stops painting it in the DOM; shader (animated) backgrounds stay web-rendered and force the CSS tier.
   - Background changes (the `background:apply` view event / BACKGROUND action) re-pipe on change.
2. **Chat sheet adoption.** On the native tier with a native-hosted wallpaper:
   - The inset sheet drops its CSS `backdrop-filter` + fill (keeps rim + sheen overlays, exactly the `GlassSurface` contract) and attaches a `GlassBridge` region at the sheet's rect.
   - **Rest-anchored, CSS during drags:** attach/update on detent settle (spring rest), detach (or freeze) during active drags and fall back to the CSS material for the drag's duration — the bridge rect sync is per-call, not per-frame, and the iOS `updateRect` animates 0.15s. This keeps 60fps drags off the JS→native bridge entirely.
   - Full-bleed stays opaque web paint (nothing to see through; no blur to save).
3. **Pill + menus** adopt `GlassSurface` the same way once the wallpaper is native (they are stable chrome — the primitive's intended anchors).
4. **Perf proof.** Before/after GPU/battery numbers on device for the dragged sheet (the #9141 measurement path), plus frame-time traces during drag on both tiers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `setBackdrop` piped end-to-end on iOS + Android with image backgrounds; shader backgrounds cleanly stay on the CSS tier (no black holes, ever).
- [ ] Chat sheet renders real `UIGlassEffect` on an iOS 26 device/sim and the Material panel on an Android 12+ device/emu, over the piped wallpaper, at every detent; CSS tier during drags with no visible pop at the handoff.
- [ ] Web/desktop/older-OS fall back to the current CSS glass with zero visual change.
- [ ] XCUITest + Android e2e legs assert the tier attribute + screenshot the sheet at rest and mid-drag on both platforms (per-platform capture per CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Frame-time/battery before/after captured and attached.

## Constraints

- No second glass primitive — everything goes through `packages/ui/src/glass/` (`GlassSurface`/`useNativeGlass`).
- One content-addressed media store — the wallpaper pipe reuses `/api/media/<sha256>` URLs, no new file store (#8876).
- Error policy: bridge failures degrade to the CSS tier via the existing `isNativeGlassAvailable` probe (J4) — never a black region.

Refs: #13560 (views epic), #9141 (backdrop-blur battery gate), the GlassBridge parity PR.4f:T4b0,## Problem

## Safety

No manual DB write, global image pin, ad-hoc systemd override/restart, or rollback bypass. The failed job is rollback-safe/pre-cutover.59:T1005,## Summary

Dedicated-agent provisioning is running the **cold path** in prod (~30–120s typical, up to ~11 min worst case) because the **warm pool is empty**: `WARM_POOL_ENABLED` is not set on the `eliza-provisioning-worker` daemon host, so `WarmPoolManager.replenish()` early-returns a no-op and the pool never refills. The replenish **wiring** was already fixed and deployed (#15310 / `b17fbbc7048`, in prod since the 2026-07-13 promote) — this is the remaining **config half**.

cc @0xSolace — your warm-pool lane (you authored the replenish fix). Diagnosed via read-only prod inspection (daemon journal + DB). **Zero code needed — two config settings.**

## Verified evidence

- `warmPoolEnabled()` defaults **false** — `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/config/containers-env.ts:647-651` (`raw === "true" || raw === "1"`).
- `WARM_POOL_ENABLED` is set truthy **nowhere in the repo or deploy config** — not in `wrangler.toml` `[vars]`/`[env.staging.vars]`/`[env.production.vars]`, not in any workflow. Read/tested only.
- On the provisioning-worker daemon host it is **absent from the daemon EnvironmentFile** (grep = 0, incl. the two most recent backups) → `replenish()` is a silent no-op (`agent-warm-pool.ts` → `"WARM_POOL_ENABLED=false (no-op)"`), and the log line is gated on `created>0||failed>0`, so nothing surfaces.
- **Prod DB: zero warm-pool rows** (`agent_sandboxes` has no `pool_status` entries). The Worker-side claim (`.../provision/route.ts:172`) therefore returns null and cold-paths regardless.
- The break is confessed in-code at `packages/scripts/cloud/admin/daemons/provisioning-worker.ts:1038-1046` ("THIS IS THE MISSING CALLER…"). The wiring fix `b17fbbc7048` is deployed; the enable flag most plausibly lived only in the retired control-plane sidecar's env and was never carried onto the daemon host.

## Fix — two settings, both required (A fills, B claims)

**A) Daemon (fills the pool):** set `WARM_POOL_ENABLED=true` in the provisioning-worker daemon's EnvironmentFile + restart → `processPoolReplenishCycle` (`provisioning-worker.ts:1730-1747`) fills within one infra-maintenance cycle (burst-limited to 3/cycle). Add the key to the daemon deploy workflow's env reconcile list so a control-plane re-arm can't silently drop it again (the #15160 drift class).

**B) Worker (claims at provision time):** add `WARM_POOL_ENABLED = "true"` as a **committed var** in `wrangler.toml [env.production.vars]` + deploy — **committed, not a dashboard secret** (`wrangler.toml:533-538` documents dashboard secrets getting wiped on Worker redeploys, which already silently re-closed apps-deploy once and is the likely cause of the original disappearance).

Either half alone leaves provisioning cold.

## Adjacent follow-ups (not the pool fix)

- The provisioning-worker daemon OOM-restarts under a 1024MB heap cap (frequent `Reached heap limit` fatals, clustered in ~6-hourly storms). Separate reliability issue — raise the heap and persist the mitigation out of ephemeral `/run/systemd`. It can intermittently trip the fail-closed heartbeat check and 503 creates, but it is **not** why the pool is empty (cycles complete between restarts and still create nothing with the flag off).
- `WarmPoolManager.healthCheck()` and `rollout()` have **no live caller** anywhere — stuck (10-min) and stale-image pool entries are never reaped. Consider wiring `healthCheck()` into a daemon phase.

## Ownership / suggested sequence

Half A is a prod ops action (env + restart; money surface — worth a sizing nod on how many warm containers to hold). Half B is a Worker PR + promote (your lane; carries the dashboard-secret-wipe redeploy risk). Suggested order: **A** (verify the pool fills via journal `warm pool replenish cycle complete` + DB `pool_status` rows) → **B** → confirm a test dedicated create claims warm (seconds instead of minutes).

Happy to do Half A and open the Half-B `wrangler.toml` PR if you want it off your plate — your call on the lane.

# Risks

**Large.** This is a broad foundation PR (297 files) spanning calendar source
identity, availability, recurrence/timezone behavior, native Apple permission
semantics, Google watch lifecycle, immutable approval and mutation receipts,
household resource capacity, personal-assistant domains, one shared scheduler,
connector contracts, UI, benchmark provenance, and a SQL migration.

Primary risks are incorrect authority or tenant binding, duplicated external
effects during retry, recurrence/DST mistakes, stale source truth, webhook
abuse, accidental data disclosure across households/calendars, native
permission-mode drift, and UI states that hide a partial provider failure. The
new paths fail closed, use source/tenant/version/idempotency bindings, and have
focused real-PGlite and contract coverage; live providers remain a draft gate.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Adds the full world-traveling co-parent persona and G1-G48 test catalog, plus
  a 12,792-word implementation report grounded in 31 official, research,
  safety, and first-person sources.
- Adds source-aware calendar availability across selected Google, Apple,
  Microsoft, and ICS feeds, including health/freshness/provenance and explicit
  partial/error states.
- Adds durable Google push-channel bindings, strict notification validation,
  dedupe/order checks, scheduled retries and renewals, restart reconstruction,
  quota classification, and controlled 410 resync.
- Adds immutable calendar mutation proposals, exact owner/editor routing,
  approval CAS, replay receipts, series/version/tenant/source binding, Apple
  add-only semantics, and truthful invitation decline behavior.
- Adds deterministic caregiver/vehicle/restraint capacity solving with
  authorization, accessibility, freshness, handoff, transition,
  distinct-resource, invalidation, and shared-review constraints.
- Extends one shared `ScheduledTask` architecture and typed dispatch results; it
  does not add a second scheduler.
- Adds school-source reconciliation, household operations, family
  communications, food/inventory, parenting guidance,
  weather/routes/activity oracle, and childcare/work-scenario foundations with
  explicit source and safety contracts.
- Adds a calendar source manager UI and native permission presentation, plus
  desktop/mobile screenshots and a walkthrough harness.
- Fixes LifeOpsBench acting-agent provenance so adapter/provider/model are
  distinct from evaluator/judge identity and incomplete artifacts are rejected.

## What kind of change is this?

Features, improvements, tests, documentation, and one additive database
migration.

68:T12a8,Closes #11670

## Root cause

`useChatSend`'s post-turn reconcile (`loadConversationMessages`) **full-replaces** the thread with server truth. When the server never persisted the user's turn — a send during local-model warm-up where the runtime-ready hold expired (`503 Agent is not running` from `conversation-routes.ts`; the user message is only persisted *after* runtime resolution), or a stream that completed empty with nothing persisted — the reload returned a thread **without** the user's message and silently evicted the optimistic bubble. No failed state, no notice on the empty-success variant, text unrecoverable. The suite never caught it because its `loadConversationMessages` mock was a no-op `{ ok: true }` instead of the real full-replace.

## Fix (root cause, no fallback sludge)

- **`restoreEvictedUserTurn()`** — after every post-send reconcile, detect that the just-sent user turn is missing from server truth (text match among user turns no older than the send minus 60s clock-skew slack, so an identical message from an *earlier* exchange can't mask an eviction) and re-attach the user's bubble **plus a retryable failed assistant turn** (`failureKind: "provider_issue"` → the overlay's existing Retry chip). The send fails loudly; one tap re-delivers once the model is ready — mirroring the existing `reattachInterruptedPartial` pattern for assistant partials.
- Wired into both reload sites of `runQueuedChatSend` (success + non-404 error path) and both sites of `sendActionMessage`. Validation-4xx rejects excluded (their draft goes back to the composer — re-attaching would duplicate). No-op when the server persisted the turn or the reload never replaced local state.
- `handleChatRetry` fallback now also drops the optimistic (`temp-`) user turn it retries, so the resend's fresh optimistic bubble doesn't transiently duplicate the message.

6c:T1324,Closes #11612.

On-device local LLM on iPhone 16 Pro Max (A18 Pro) crash-looped: `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0` in `ggml_metal_encoder_set_pipeline` during the first `llama_decode`, ~32 s after every launch, 4/4 launches (`.github/issue-evidence/xplatform-ios-device/prefix-App-2026-07-02-182502.ips` and siblings).

## The fix (three parts + root cause)

**1. Recoverable Metal failure** — llama.cpp fork submodule → `58c0391ebbe` (branch [`fix/11612-metal-nil-pipeline-recoverable`](https://github.com/elizaOS/llama.cpp/tree/fix/11612-metal-nil-pipeline-recoverable) on `elizaOS/llama.cpp`). A nil compute pipeline no longer aborts the process: the encoder latches the failure, the op skips encoding, and `ggml_metal_graph_compute` returns `GGML_STATUS_FAILED`, so `llama_decode` surfaces a catchable error (clean error / cloud fallback — no crash-loop). `GGML_METAL_ABORT_ON_NIL_PIPELINE=1` restores the old abort for debugging. This supersedes develop's previous gitlink `299d5b78b` (abort-only guard); the new tip is a clean superset that also carries the non-Apple kokoro fast path + converter work already on the fork branch.

**2. GGML log file sink** — iOS doesn't forward the embedded engine's stdio, so the `GGML_LOG_ERROR` naming the failing kernel was unobservable. `runtime-symbol-shim.c eliza_llama_log_to_file` + `LlamaBridgeImpl installGgmlLogSink` now append ggml/llama logs line-flushed to `$ELIZA_STATE_DIR/logs/ggml.log`, pullable with `xcrun devicectl device copy from`. This sink is what captured the root cause below.

**3. Jetsam memory budget** — `LlamaBridgeImpl.loadModel` measures `os_proc_available_memory()` before loading, halves context/KV down to 1024 to fit, and fails cleanly with a memory error when even the minimum cannot fit; the iOS JS bridge (`plugin-capacitor-bridge/src/ios/bridge.ts`) pre-flights model size vs available RAM before starting a multi-minute native load.

**bf16 root cause** (found via the new log sink): the iOS embedded metallib was compiled at `-std=ios-metal2.4`, and `ggml-metal.metal` `#if`'s the whole bf16 kernel family out below `__METAL_VERSION__ 310` — so `kernel_mul_mm_bf16_f32` was missing from the library while the A18 GPU-family probe still set `has_bfloat=true` and selected it for eliza-1's bf16 tensors → `MTLLibraryError Code=5`, every decode graph dead. Fix chain:
- `build-llama-cpp-mtp.mjs`: default `ELIZA_IOS_METAL_STD` `ios-metal2.4` → `metal3.1` (raises the AIR floor to iOS 17; on iOS 16 the embedded library fails to load and Metal cleanly degrades to CPU).
- submodule `58c0391ebbe`: gate `has_bfloat` on the loaded library **actually containing** the bf16 kernels, not just the GPU family.
- `build-xcframework.mjs`: packaging audit that hard-fails if `kernel_mul_mm_bf16_f32` is missing from a slice — this regression class can't ship silently again.

## On-device retest (same physical device, rebuilt + redeployed each leg)

- **Crash-loop: GONE, device-verified.** Post-fix: **zero new `App-*.ips`** across ~20 min / two launches including full model load + the first `llama_decode` (the exact pre-fix crash point) — the decode failure is logged and surfaced instead. Evidence: [`11612-fix-retest/`](../tree/fix/11612-ios-metal-recoverable-bf16/.github/issue-evidence/xplatform-ios-device/11612-fix-retest) (README, soak screenshots t+60→780 s, `ggml-device.log`, crash-baseline vs final crash-list diff).
- **bf16 kernel: RESOLVED on device.** After the MSL 3.1 rebuild, `kernel_mul_mm_bf16_f32` compiles and loads on the A18 (`ggml_metal_library_compile_pipeline: loaded kernel_mul_mm_bf16_f32_… th_max = 1024`), zero missing-kernel errors in the new session, zero new app crash reports. Evidence: [`11612-bf16-retest/`](../tree/fix/11612-ios-metal-recoverable-bf16/.github/issue-evidence/xplatform-ios-device/11612-bf16-retest) (README, `ggml-device-postfix.log`, `mtp-slice-capabilities.json` packaging audit PASS).
- **Known residual (separate product work, quantified in the bf16 README):** generation on the 8 GB phone is still blocked by GPU OOM — a 4.63 GB fp16-class GGUF at `n_gpu_layers: 999` + `n_ubatch` 1024 demands ~5.8 GiB against a 5.46 GiB Metal working-set budget. Needs device-aware offload/ubatch admission (iOS has no `assessFit` equivalent) and/or a phone-tier quant + unload-on-decode-failure. The app no longer crashes: the failure is a clean logged error.

## Evidence

`.github/issue-evidence/xplatform-ios-device/` (in this PR): pre-fix crash `.ips` + JetsamEvent + device console/syslog + STT wav, `11612-fix-retest/` and `11612-bf16-retest/` with per-run READMEs, timelines, build-provenance (build-is-mine greps), screenshots, and pulled `ggml.log`s.

73:T8ce,## What

Upgrades `@biomejs/biome` from **2.4.16 → 2.5.1** (latest stable) across the entire workspace and reformats the tree to 2.5.1's canonical style.

## Why

The workspace had a **biome version skew**: `package.json` files declared a mix of `2.4.16`, `2.5.0`, and `^2.4.14`, while `bun.lock` (and therefore CI's `bun install --frozen-lockfile`) resolved **2.4.16**. Because PR CI lint is path-gated (it only lints changed files), 2.5.x-formatted files merged via PRs that didn't touch them could slip in and then fail a full repo `bun run lint`. Pinning one version everywhere removes that whole class of intermittent lint drift.

## Changes

**Commit 1 — version bump (config only):**
- Pin `@biomejs/biome` to `2.5.1` in all **97** `package.json` files
- Regenerate `bun.lock` (resolves `2.4.16` → `2.5.1`)
- Bump `$schema` to `2.5.1` in all **68** `biome.json` configs
- Migrate the deprecated `linter.rules.recommended: true` → `linter.rules.preset: "recommended"` in **50** configs (behavior-identical; removes the 2.5.x deprecation diagnostic)

**Commit 2 — mechanical reformat:**
- `biome check --write` under the 2.5.1 toolchain (formatting + organizeImports only — **no logic changes**). The bulk of the diff is the trailing-comma behavior change between 2.4 and 2.5.

## Verification

- **Per-package lint green at 2.5.1:** serial sweep of all no-write first-party packages → **51 pass, 0 needing fixes, 0 residual lint errors**.
- `packages/core` typechecks clean (the reformat is format + import-ordering, which cannot change types).
- All `biome.json` configs validate at 2.5.1 (no `deserialize`/deprecation diagnostics; verified core/agent/app).

## Notes for the reviewer

- This is a large (~1100-file) **mechanical** change. The meaningful review surface is **commit 1** (versions + config). Commit 2 is pure formatter output.
- It's a repo-wide reformat, so it can go stale against an active `develop`. If it can't fast-forward at merge time, the cleanest sync is to **regenerate** rather than rebase: `bun install` then `bunx @biomejs/biome check --write .` on the latest `develop`. (At open time it rebased onto `develop` with **zero** conflicts.)

79:Tcf1,Closes #13537.

## What
Makes the notification remote-push path a **live** pipeline. The server-side APNs/FCM stack (`NotificationPushService`, `ApnsProvider`, `FcmProvider`, `PushTokenRegistry`, `/api/notifications/push-tokens` routes) was already built but **dead**: no client ever registered a device token, so `PushTokenRegistry.list()` was always empty and `onNotification` returned early every time (rule-10: endpoint with no client trigger).

This PR adds the missing client leg and proves the loop end-to-end:

- `ElizaClient.registerPushToken(platform, token)` / `unregisterPushToken(token)` (`packages/ui/src/api/client-notifications.ts`) — the real client trigger for the push-token routes.
- `packages/ui/src/state/notifications/push-registration.ts` — acquires the OS remote token via `@capacitor/push-notifications` `register()` + `registration` listener and POSTs it, gated on a **granted** notification permission (native-only; no-op on web/desktop). Tapped pushes deep-link through the same scheme-checked `navigateDeepLink` as the in-app center.

While running the real gemma-4-31b benchmark review for #10199/#10193, two model-independent runtime bugs surfaced that made whole benchmark lanes score 0.0. This PR fixes them and lands the reviewed evidence.

## Bug 1 — standard-suite (MMLU/GSM8K/HumanEval/MT-Bench) scored 0.0

Every reply was the runtime apology text; server stderr showed
`Trajectory limit exceeded: terminal_only_continuations (3/2)`. Five compounding causes, all fixed:
- **evaluator** (`packages/core/src/runtime/evaluator.ts`): a FINISH after a terminal-only planner step with a real terminal message was coerced to CONTINUE, tripping the trajectory limit after 3 identical answers → apology. Now stays FINISH.
- **bench-server prompt** (`server-utils.ts`): dedicated `composeStandardSuitePrompt` — the generic "BENCHMARK CONTEXT" trailer made Stage-1 route exam MCQs into tools.
- **message stage-1** (`services/message.ts`): `isTextScoredBenchmarkTurn` vetoes hard-forcing a non-terminal tool call for text-scored suites.
- **bench plugin**: `BENCHMARK_ACTION` disabled for the standard suite (its ANSWER/GUESS similes lured the planner).
- **orchestrator** (`adapters.py`, `runner.py`): smoke `max_tokens` 256→2048 (GSM8K CoT truncation); integer `sample` now maps to `limit`.

**Proof:** mmlu 0.0 → 0.75, gsm8k 0.0 → 1.0 (gemma-4-31b live, sample=8). Regression test added.

## Bug 2 — media-reply sanitizer flattened multiline replies

`sanitizeReplyTextAfterMediaDelivery` ran `\s{2,}` → " " on EVERY reply (\s matches newline), flattening code/lists/paragraphs to one line even with no media. Surfaced via HumanEval: every completion lost its newlines → SyntaxError. Now returns media-free replies untouched and collapses only same-line gaps. **humaneval 0.35 → 0.75.**

develop still ships a **dismissable** onboarding chat with a **live composer**

### Programmable GLSL shader background (#10694)
develop already had undo/redo; this adds the arbitrary programmable shader mode:
- `ProgrammableShaderBackground` renders a GLSL fragment via **raw three.js**
  (already a dep; no new deps) behind a full safety sandbox for untrusted GPU
  code: compile-validate before showing, clamped uniforms, frame-time watchdog,
  WebGL context-loss recovery, reduced-motion static frame, and a color-field
  fallback on any failure (a bad shader can never white-screen or hang the app);
- `BackgroundConfig` gains a `glsl` mode (source + presetId + typed/clamped
  uniforms); `normalizeBackgroundConfig` collapses a hostile/oversized/absent
  source to the color field on load;
- 5-preset GLSL library (aurora/lava/plasma/waves/nebula, bounded loops only);
- BACKGROUND action drives it from chat: named presets (+ synonyms), a generic
  "animated shader" → default, and relative tweaks (slower/brighter/bigger),
  with precedence so "red brighter" stays red and "molten" beats a bare color.

## What this does

Ports the [Vexa](https://github.com/Vexa-ai/vexa) (Apache-2.0) meeting-bot stack **into the elizaOS plugin system** — no separate deployment. The agent joins **Google Meet / Microsoft Teams / Zoom** meetings as an anonymous guest, captures per-speaker audio in the browser, transcribes it through the runtime model layer (`ModelType.TRANSCRIPTION`), attributes speakers by DOM-based diarization, and lands live, diarized transcripts in the existing **Transcripts view** and **knowledge store**. **Discord** voice channels get the same treatment (per-user SSRC = exact diarization). Works fully **local** (no cloud, no OAuth), hybrid, and fully **cloud** (metered `/api/v1/voice/stt`).

## Architecture

New **`@elizaos/plugin-meetings`** — one engine, per-platform strategy classes (Vexa's proven `PlatformStrategies` shape):

- **platforms/** — ported bot adapters (Meet/Teams/Zoom): guest join, admission (reCAPTCHA-stay), removal, leave, verbatim Vexa selectors; `playwright-core` stealth launch; pluggable humanized input (Playwright min-jerk trajectories / Linux XTEST). Browser audio capture: per-element 16 kHz `ScriptProcessor` via `exposeBinding`.
- **pipeline/** — `SpeakerStreamManager` (LocalAgreement-2 confirmation, 2s cadence / 30s cap / 15s idle), ASR via `useModel(TRANSCRIPTION)` with retry/backoff, verbatim multi-language hallucination corpus, `TranscriptSegment` assembly + retained session mix.
- **service.ts** — session state machine (single bot per meeting, room/world/entity wiring), `JOIN_MEETING`/`LEAVE_MEETING`/`GET_MEETING_TRANSCRIPT` actions, `/api/meetings` routes, `ACTIVE_MEETINGS` provider, live `meeting-status`/`meeting-transcript` WS envelopes via the existing `connector-setup` broadcast seam (no `packages/agent` change).

Storage reuses the existing transcript subsystem (#8789): records land in the `transcripts` memory partition **and** mirror to the documents/knowledge store, so `/api/transcripts` + the Transcripts view render meeting transcripts with zero extra wiring (golden-tested against the view reader).

**Integrations:**
- **plugin-discord** — voice-channel meeting transcripts: tees each speaker's decoded PCM into the pipeline; `/transcribe start|stop`; `DISCORD_VOICE_TRANSCRIPTS` gate (default off); existing utterance-reply/barge-in/TTS untouched.
- **plugin-elizacloud** — registers the previously-dormant `handleTranscription` so `useModel(TRANSCRIPTION)` arbitrates local-first with Eliza Cloud fallback; `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_USE_STT` gate mirroring the TTS gate.
- **plugin-calendar / plugin-google** — meeting auto-join via the frozen `ScheduledTask` spine (`relative_to_anchor` on `calendar_event`, anchors follow reschedules; `off|ask|all` policy); Google `conferenceData` fix (prefer video entry point over dial-in); "Send agent to meeting" + in-meeting badge in the calendar views.
- **packages/ui** — Transcripts view gains a paste-URL Join bar, live confirmed+pending pane over the agent WS, platform/participant metadata on meeting records.

Local-only: anonymous guest join + local fused ASR, zero cloud/OAuth. Telegram group-call audio is **not** reachable via the Bot API (no tgcalls) — documented limitation, MTProto is future work.

Attribution: `NOTICE` file credits Vexa.ai (Apache-2.0).

## Testing

88:T1361,## What

Upstreams the **visual LOOK layer** of the `feat/ui-overhaul` branch (#13069) that never landed. Overnight ~all of the overhaul's mechanics + token plumbing merged (57 PRs), but the actual aesthetic did not. This makes stock `develop` look like the polished build.

## Root cause the look never landed (found + fixed)

The overhaul put its ember token system into `theme.css` **and** `base.css`, but the running app only imports `base.css` + `tailwind-theme.css` (via `styles.css`) — `theme.css` is loaded **only** by the e2e fixture bundler. So on stock `develop`, every already-shipped `bg-scrim` / `bg-card` (=`--surface-1`) usage (`NotificationCenter`, `drawer`, …) resolved to an **undefined token → transparent at runtime**. This PR lands the token layer in `base.css` (+ a runtime `--scrim` in both themes), so those usages resolve for real.

8a:Ta38,## Problem (ISO build layer 7)

With layers 1-6 fixed (arch gate, ERR trap, setup-bun, branding, source + dist overlay patches — #15223/#15226/#15232/#15250/#15285), the re-dispatched **Build elizaOS Linux ISO** run cleared the overlay-prep step and reached `just build` -> `build.sh` -> `build-iso.sh`, where it failed on **both arches**:

```
no .git in source tree — initializing a throwaway repo for the build
dpkg-parsechangelog: error: cannot open file debian/changelog: No such file or directory
error: Recipe `build` failed on line 154 with exit code 25
```

## Root cause

`packages/os/linux/tails/debian/changelog` is a **required vendored-Tails source input**, not a build artifact:

- `build-iso.sh` seeds the previous-release git tag from it (`dpkg-parsechangelog --offset 1`) when building from the tag-less vendored snapshot;
- `tails/auto/config` copies it into the ISO docs (`cp debian/changelog .../doc/tails/Changelog`);
- `tails/Changelog` is a **symlink** to it (dangling without it);
- it matches the pinned **Tails 7.8** snapshot the rest of `tails/` is cut from.

It was committed in the elizaOS baseline, but the wholesale `.gitignore` regenerated by the develop history rewrite (#14459) added a `/packages/os/linux/tails/debian/changelog` line — lumping this required source in with the large generated/binary files that auto-generated rule-list drops (PDFs, PNGs, CSVs). So a fresh CI checkout no longer contains it. `tails/` is not a submodule and **no generator or fetch step exists** anywhere — the file is simply meant to be present.

## Fix

Restore the exact file from the baseline blob and drop the erroneous ignore rule.

## Validation

Locally, the exact failing call now succeeds against the restored file:

```
$ cd packages/os/linux/tails
$ dpkg-parsechangelog -SVersion               # current
7.8
$ dpkg-parsechangelog --offset 1 --count 1 -SVersion | tr '~' '-'   # the failing call
7.7.2
```

The `tails/Changelog` symlink resolves and the `auto/config` cp source exists. Full ~1.5h ISO assembly re-dispatched on develop after merge (amd64 required; arm64 continue-on-error).

## Heads-up (not fixed here, likely future layers)

The same `.gitignore` rewrite also dropped several `tails/wiki` **media/font assets** (`*.mp4`, `*.ttf`, `.png` under `wiki/src/lib` and `wiki/src/install/inc`). Those are website/wiki build inputs and may surface as a later ikiwiki-website layer if the release build doesn't skip the site. Flagging for owner awareness rather than speculatively re-committing binaries.

# Risks

Medium-to-large in blast radius, risk-reducing in direction. This changes a production deploy path under `.github/workflows`, so it needs human review and must not be auto-merged. It does not weaken any existing check; every change either tightens a boundary or holds it. The operational surface that changes is the release runbook (operators now dispatch from `develop` with a `candidate_run_id` instead of dispatching from the candidate branch), so a release operator should confirm that flow before the next promotion.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

### [P1] Candidate-controlled workflow code entered the production-secret job

A manually selected candidate SHA supplied `.github/workflows/eliza-computer.yml` and every deployment script, and the job then entered the production environment and received Cloudflare credentials. The admission check ran *inside* the candidate-controlled definition, so the candidate could modify or bypass the check meant to gate it. Human environment approval reduced likelihood but was not a code-enforced trust boundary.

The deploy job now:

- checks out `refs/heads/develop` and verifies through the API that the checkout is current `origin/develop`;
- rejects any `production-candidate` dispatch from a ref other than `develop`;
- accepts a candidate's build **by run identity** through a new `candidate_run_id` input, replacing `candidate_pr`.

The candidate contributes exactly one thing: the immutable artifact built by the secretless `quality` job. The protected admission step requires that run to be completed, successful, same-repository, not `pull_request`/`pull_request_target`, and a run of *this* workflow file, and requires its head SHA to be the current head of an open same-repository PR into `develop` that is zero commits behind a freshly fetched `origin/develop`. Deploy metadata, byte verification, and the Cloudflare commit hash all bind to the admitted bundle SHA.

Side benefit: because a candidate branch is never dispatched directly, the `eliza-army-production` deployment-branch allowlist keeps `develop` as its only entry and no longer needs the temporary-allowlist step the old runbook described.

### [P1] Production resolved Wrangler outside `bun.lock`

The job ran `bunx wrangler@4.100.0` *after* entering the production environment, so the secret-bearing lane could re-resolve executable content from a registry at deploy time. Per the correction on #17424, wrangler was already in `bun.lock` via the root override; the defect was that the job never installed from the lock and never invoked the installed binary.

Now: `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --filter @elizaos/eliza-computer`, then execute `packages/eliza-computer/node_modules/.bin/wrangler` for both the project-create and deploy paths. A preceding step asserts the binary reports the pinned version and fails **before** any credential is used. `wrangler@4.100.0` becomes an explicit `@elizaos/eliza-computer` devDependency matching the existing root override, which adds exactly one line to `bun.lock`.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fixes (security boundary repair in CI/CD), plus the documentation that describes the corrected release procedure.

## Two-project topology (re: the #17413 "packages/homepage/dist" note)

`eliza.army` and `eliza.app` are **separate** Cloudflare Pages projects and this deploy does not fight the existing homepage topology:

- `eliza-computer.yml` → project `eliza-computer` → `eliza.army`, built from `packages/eliza-computer` (standalone Vite site, `wrangler.toml` owns `pages_build_output_dir = "./dist"`).
- `deploy-homepage.yml` → project `eliza-app-home` → `eliza.app`, built from `packages/homepage`.

Their `paths:` filters are disjoint, so neither can preempt or overwrite the other. Documented in `packages/eliza-computer/AGENTS.md` so the two projects are not conflated later.

# Documentation changes needed?

Done in this PR. `packages/eliza-computer/AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` carry the corrected release runbook and the two-project topology; `.github/workflows/CHANGELOG.md` records the CI policy change.

`.github/workflows/eliza-computer.yml`, the `deploy:` job. Read it as a security boundary: confirm nothing executed in that job originates from the candidate ref, and that no credential is referenced before the admission and wrangler-version steps have passed. Then read `packages/eliza-computer/scripts/deployment-contract.test.mjs`, which is what keeps those properties from regressing.

The install path, the wrangler resolution, and every admission predicate are verified above against real payloads and a real frozen install; the remaining unverified step is the Cloudflare API call itself, which is unchanged apart from which binary invokes it and which SHA it binds to.

# Deploy Notes

The release runbook changes. Operators no longer dispatch from the candidate branch; they dispatch from `develop` with `release_mode=production-candidate` and `candidate_run_id` set to the candidate's already-finished `quality` run. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are updated to match. The `eliza-army-production` deployment-branch allowlist should keep `develop` as its only entry.

`permissions:` gains `actions: read` so the protected job can inspect the candidate run and download its artifact cross-run.
