# Critical review outcome

The original implementation was not safe to merge. It treated positive
authorization values in eventually consistent KV as a revocation boundary,
used unbounded Durable Object calls on the request path, swallowed alarm
recovery failures, did not scope one recovery lookup by tenant, and described
mocked Durable Object tests as integration coverage.

This revision separates authorization from admission:

- `INFERENCE_AUTH_CACHE_ENABLED` is independent and defaults to `false` in
  every checked-in environment.
- With that flag off, populated positive KV entries are ignored and origin
  authorization remains authoritative.
- The exact rate/spend Durable Object admission and revisioned accounting
  foundations can soak without enabling unsafe cached authorization.
- Authorization caching must remain off until #17093 provides a strongly
  consistent revocation boundary and immutable Steward session identity.

This is therefore a staged architectural foundation, not approval to enable
the complete cache-only hot path in production.

# What changes

- Covers `/v1/chat`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`,
  `/v1/responses`, `/v1/embeddings`, shared-agent turns, and the internal
  voice-session Eliza LLM turn.
- Adds revisioned authorization, pricing, policy, and balance projections.
- Adds per-organization Durable Objects for exact rate limiting and monetary
  leases, dispatch marking, settlement, and alarm recovery.
- Adds revision-aware, idempotent accounting and anonymous-inference recovery.
- Bounds admission-gate rate, lease, release, settlement, and dispatch calls;
  stalled admission fails closed.
- Makes alarm recovery failures observable and rethrows an aggregate failure
  so Cloudflare retries the alarm.
- Scopes recovery app lookup by both app ID and organization ID.
- Runs the production Durable Object in Miniflare/workerd with real storage and
  proves concurrent $7 leases against a $10 balance admit exactly one request.
- Adds the required Durable Object and rate-limiter bindings (with
  `new_sqlite_classes` migrations) in the default, staging, and production
  environments. Relies on the existing staging/production `CACHE_KV`
  namespaces; no KV binding is added, and the top-level dev environment
  still has no `CACHE_KV`.

Direct STT, TTS, and voice-clone media/job endpoints remain outside scope.

# Risk and rollout

**Deploy ordering:** the hot-path snapshot read selects
`organizations.balance_revision`, so migrations 0177-0181 must apply before or
with the Worker deploy (the deploy workflow's migration step already runs
first — keep that ordering). `INFERENCE_BILLING_LEDGER` flips `""` -> `"db"`
in all environments in this PR: it takes effect on staging with the next
develop deploy (the intended soak) and on production only via a later
main deploy, which stays gated on the #17096 evidence.

**Large / money path.** This changes admission, reservation, crash recovery,
settlement, affiliate payout, and balance projection. Require cloud/billing
owner review.

The warm path has serial Durable Object operations before provider dispatch.
Each client operation is bounded by a 1.5 second abort timeout. The included
benchmark is in-process and does not claim deployed Cloudflare latency.

Do not enable cached authorization or broadly adopt the route path until the
dependent issues above are complete and staging supplies rollback, latency,
revocation, recovery, and accounting evidence.

# Post-rebase deep review (five-dimension) — addendum

A five-dimension adversarial review (DO money path, auth-cache safety,
revisioned accounting, route integration, test realness) was run against this
branch after the rebase; every post-rebase CI failure was root-caused, and the
following landed on the branch (see the review comment for the full report):

- Sub-ledger-unit creator movements are a designed `below_ledger_unit` outcome
  (consumer charge proceeds, nothing recorded, auditable) instead of failing
  the reservation; creator-movement replays are first-committed-wins on keyed
  dedupe with identity fields strictly validated and a committed-row
  direction cross-check.
- Balance snapshot reads moved to a typed repository seam; the fail-closed
  balance tests now run against real PGlite with the real 0177 trigger and
  real corrupt values (`'NaN'::numeric`, NULL) — no mocked seams.
- Dead money-path modules removed (`createDeferredAdmissionSettler`,
  `recoverInferenceChargeViaLedger`); the DB-ledger settle now returns the
  real settlement transaction id.
- Session-path IAC cache writes are gated on `INFERENCE_AUTH_CACHE_ENABLED`
  (matching the API-key path); shared-agent session scope-cache hits
  revalidate `is_active`/org identity/org active from the lifecycle-
  invalidated user cache; cache validators are mutually exclusive.
- Streaming `onFinish` with absent usage settles at the admitted estimate,
  never $0 for delivered output; `/v1/chat` gained the stream settlement
  backstop; the messages-route terminal enqueue is guarded.

## Known limitations (tracked follow-ups)

- Shared-runtime local failures thrown before `onProviderDispatch` settle
  conservatively at the estimate; propagating a "dispatch never reached" flag
  would make zero provable (#17094).
- Negative shared-agent scope entries serve cached 401/403/404 for up to the
  30 s base TTL; mutation-side invalidation would remove that window (#17093).
- `uncollectedDebtUsd` in the gate DO only grows (no repayment interplay), and
  a corrupt-invariant alarm throw can freeze recovery for that org's leases
  until manual intervention; both are availability-direction, not money-loss,
  and belong to #17094/#17095.
- Only the lease/lease race runs under real workerd; settle/dispatch/release/
  alarm and the AnonymousChatGate DO are covered by in-memory-storage unit
  suites (#17094).

## Headline: iOS on-device model download (#11841)
- **keep-awake during download** — reference-counted `keep_awake_set` that holds the iOS idle timer open while a model download is active, so auto-lock can't suspend the in-process transfer. Wired on **both** engine paths: the JSContext compat bridge *and* the full-Bun `host_call` dispatch (`FullBunEngineHost`), with the JavaScriptCore-free core split so it compiles into the full-Bun target. Verified on-device: BUILD SUCCEEDED + installed on an iPhone 16 Pro Max running the full-Bun engine; the `host_call` path is live (`host call method=…`). Downloader unit tests 20/20.

Removed "recommended" from the cloud signal (cloud still matches on cloud/eliza cloud/online); added a regression test (first-run 22/22).

91:T16bb,## Summary

Overhauls the Milady chat surface across web, iOS, Android, and desktop, and lands a **native chat-transcript renderer** (SwiftUI on iOS, Views on Android, an AppKit spike on macOS) driven by one shared, versioned contract. Renamed `ContinuousChatOverlay → ChatOverlay` throughout.

Three themes:

### 1. Liquid-glass chat surface (real OS material where physics allows)
- The chat sheet floats as liquid glass: a light fill over a heavy `backdrop-filter` (blur + saturate + brightness) so the field behind glows *through* the panel, plus the directional specular rim.
- **Native glass on Capacitor**: the `GlassBridge` plugin (iOS 26 `UIGlassEffect`, Android 12+ Material) was never registered — fixed. The default ember field moves into a **native layer behind a transparent webview** (`setBackdrop`), and the inset sheet anchors a real `UIGlassEffect` panel over it (verified live via lldb: `<UIGlassEffect: …>` + an `EmberBackdropView`/`CAGradientLayer` below the `WKWebView`). The panel's corner radius tracks the sheet's animated corners.
- Maximized chat is a flat neutral `#212121` reading surface (the sheen/gradient read as artifacts full-screen); the exit is a pure cover-layer crossfade (no discrete style swap at the corners); the maximized composer capsule is glassmorphic.
- Desktop: opt-in `NSVisualEffectView` window glass behind the chat-overlay window (`ELIZA_DESKTOP_NATIVE_GLASS=1`).

### 2. Gesture correctness (the pull continuum)
- **maximize → pull-to-half** now settles at a real detent (was: bounced tall / collapsed / stranded a stub). Root causes fixed: an invisible stale grabber captured the restore drag; the restore bookkeeping raced the maximize-release hysteresis; `maximizeFromPull` never settled the height spring (stranded the GPU layer + drag latch); restore releases free-rested instead of completing.
- One **constant pointer-locked drag handle** across pill ↔ input ↔ chat (rendered outside the scale transform, y tracks the panel's visual top).
- Restore drag morphs live (shape springs home, handle fades in under the finger) instead of popping at release.
- Regression e2e: `test:chat-restore-e2e`, `test:chat-restore-continuum-e2e`.

### 3. Native chat-transcript renderer (new)
Everything in the chat renders to **native widgets** — text/markdown, code, choice, follow-ups, form (fields/select/checkbox + validation), workflow, checklist, task card, background swatches, permission card, secret request, tool-call rows, thinking disclosure, failure/retry.

- **One contract** (`eliza.native-transcript/v1`): frames serialized through the *same* `parseSegments` the DOM uses; a typed action envelope back (`message | navigate | prefill | background | retry`). A golden fixture is conformance-tested by every decoder.
- **iOS** SwiftUI, **Android** Views, **macOS** AppKit spike — all one contract.
- Security by construction: secrets are display-only (never transit chat/bridge), permission grant requires a real OS request (no fabrication), navigate/prefill/background stay local intents (never leaked to the agent as chat text).
- Harness demo: `ELIZA_NATIVE_TRANSCRIPT_DEMO=1 bun run --cwd packages/app ios:chat-harness:preview` (full-screen native, DOM composer reserved at the bottom; `eliza:native-transcript-split=1` for side-by-side review).

## Red-team

A 4-lens adversarial red-team (security / iOS correctness / DOM-parity / bridge-lifecycle) + verification judge returned **NO-GO on 5 HIGH findings**; **all fixed** and re-verified:
- iOS scroll no longer yanks a reader who scrolled up (at-bottom guard, DOM/Android parity).
- iOS widget `@State` keyed by stable segment/tool identity, not array offset (locked choice / form draft no longer adopts the wrong view's state).
- Android row fingerprint excludes streaming-volatile fields (widget drafts/locks survive token growth).
- `navigate` routes through the real `dispatchNavigateViewEvent` shape the shell reads.
- Retry is a typed `{kind:retry}` envelope gated to retryable failure kinds (no fabricated chat string).
Plus MEDs: iOS markdown link runs stripped; Android background emits shared preset ids; Android rejects non-v1 schema; Android form no longer trims; harness hides the native list on mid-`show()` unmount; sim-check fails on a native reject.

## Validation

**iOS on-simulator** — all 14 widget types rendered natively and interactive: choice (selection state), form (text input + required validation + submit producing the exact DOM-parity `[form:submit …] {json}`), permission (no grant button), secret (display-only), follow-ups, workflow (step glyphs), tool calls (running/success + duration), thinking, checklist, task, background, code, generated-UI card, failure (gated Retry). Bridge round-trip proven (native tap → `transcriptAction` → script advance → new frame → native re-render).

**Android on-emulator** — native choice + form rendered as native Views (EditText/Spinner/CheckBox/Button); bridge round-trip confirmed in logcat.

**Automated** — 558 UI vitest; native conformance: swiftc -typecheck (0 errors, full module), decode-check, 65-check widget logic script, javac (0), JVM contract 6/6; chat-sheet e2e 296/296; restore e2es green; iOS mirror byte-identical.

## Known follow-ups (non-blocking)
- Native conformance gates (Swift/JVM) are not yet wired into CI (only the TS `spec.test.ts` runs there). Add a macOS Swift lane + JVM lane on fixture/model changes.
- Deep-nesting decode depth cap (hardening; latent, native not production-wired).
- The maximized composer is still CSS glass (an in-page sheet over DOM pixels can't be lensed by an under-webview native panel); a true-native maximized input needs the dual-webview or native-composer architecture.

Full audit and hardening of the LifeOps/PA stack (scheduling, calendar, email, reminders, todos, goals, check-ins, follow-ups, approvals) per #10721 #10723 #8795 #9310 #10757. Four parallel research audits (issues, runtime code, test corpus, optimization pipeline) produced file:line-verified findings; 41 commits land the fixes, every one with fail-without-fix regression proof.

### P0 correctness fixes (the system did not actually schedule anything)

- **Core task tick re-arm** (`1d7d008741`): the dirty-gate disarmed after the first 1s tick and `markDirty()` had zero callers — every repeat task (including the LifeOps 60s heartbeat) ran at most once per boot. 8 tests fail without the fix.
- **Recurrence made real** (`488814580d`): recurring tasks fired at most once ever (terminal-death via skip/complete + tick status filter; `fired` zombies raced forever; `acknowledged` excluded). CAS refire claim + widened partial index + refire-candidate slice. 14 tests fail without.
- **Frozen clock** (`15fe56184b`): the runner cached the first tick's `now` closure — `firedAt` was always boot time and completion timeouts became instantly due. Mutable clock ref.
- **Dispatch policy enforced** (`e7d258d3dc`, #10721 H2): typed `DispatchResult {ok:false}` was recorded as a successful fire — the user silently never received the message. Bounded retries, ladder escalation across channels, `connectorDegradation`, terminal fail + `pipeline.onFail`. 7/8 tests fail without.
- **Snooze-override indexing** (`81b625a974`): a snoozed daily reminder fired ~a day late; a snoozed `once` fell off the index entirely.
- **Heartbeat un-brick + tick isolation** (`54f45b152e`): 5 consecutive failures permanently paused LifeOps across restarts; one failing subsystem aborted the whole tick.
- **Approvals execute** (`87dccd1d71`, `79f673d4cd`, `0fce62eb2e`): approving a send/workflow/signature did NOTHING (executor discarded; dynamic worker name never registered; fake "Approved."); expired requests could be resurrected via TOCTOU in BOTH approval stores. Stable worker + CAS transitions everywhere.
- **Honest in_app dispatch** (`66e5d9d2c9`): the in-app branch fabricated `ok:true` with no live surface; delivery now counts real surfaces.
- **Fabrications deleted** (`883068c93b`, `8446a9d797`): the canned flight-conflict template (returned a scripted answer regardless of the calendar) and CONFLICT_DETECT's fake "No conflicts detected" (loader never wired); real CalendarService loader + honest `CALENDAR_UNAVAILABLE`.
- **Reminder datetimes** (`a46f9eff13`, `ac78e9875a`): "remind me Friday" fired IMMEDIATELY (extraction schema had no date field → `dueAt = now`); reschedules were silent no-ops; snooze always 30min; English-keyword vetoes broke multilingual requests. Date+time extraction via the relative resolver, clarification-not-fabrication, date-level moves.
- **LLM-tolerant trigger boundary + duplicate guard** (`7273e0d981`): found by hand-reviewing a LIVE trajectory — the model's natural trigger shapes bounced (5 failed calls) and it created duplicate reminders across turns. Aliases normalize; failures teach the canonical shape; identical active tasks dedupe.

# Risks

Medium. Snap, Debian, and Flatpak jobs now stop when an installed launcher fails, reports a different version, or lacks usable help. This can expose previously hidden packaging defects and intentionally block publication. The Flatpak metadata also replaces three dead screenshot URLs with current public 1440×900 application baselines so validation can reach the package build and launcher smoke.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds one process-level verifier for installed elizaOS launchers and uses it in all five Snap, Debian, and Flatpak smoke steps. The verifier runs the actual installed command for both `--version` and `--help`, requires a zero exit, requires the exact release version, and requires a Commander `Usage:` section.

Contract tests exercise real child executables and parse the workflow YAML to prevent masked launcher checks from returning. Flatpak AppStream metadata now points at existing reviewed application screenshots rather than deleted documentation assets.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking release-pipeline hardening).

# Documentation changes needed?

The Flatpak submission README now documents its repository-hosted screenshot source of truth.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)a3:T18a2,## Realtime voice: integrated Phase-1 slice (server + client + live-provider evidence)

One vertical slice, per Definition of Done: server, browser client, and the evidence rig that proved them against **live Deepgram Flux + Cartesia Sonic**, in a single reviewable unit. Nothing here is a seam, a stub, or UI ahead of capability.

### What this is
- **Server** (`packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/session/**`, `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/voice-session/**`): mint route (short-lived scoped JWT, jti, aud-bound), consent-nonce precondition (server-enforced, SEC-21), WS handler with hello-first headerless auth (WebView 113 cannot set WS headers), revoke-to-silence (SEC-6: revocation severs live provider sockets), server-derived usage metering (SEC-15: client never trusted for cost), interruption pipeline under a single voiceTurnId (cancel TTS -> abort SSE -> flush downlink -> `interrupted`), uplink re-framing to Flux's 2560B/80ms frames.
- **Client** (`packages/ui/src/voice/voice-session-*.ts`): mint -> hello-first WSS -> full event handling; mic capture with runtime-verified AudioWorklet + ScriptProcessor fallback (WebView 113); streaming PCM playback (no decodeAudioData full-clip barrier); barge-in flushes local playback before server ack; re-mint on revoked/expired token (no reconnect with a dead token); maps onto the existing unified voice status from #15924 (no second state system).
- **Evidence harness** (`packages/tools/voice-evidence-harness`): one command drives baseline / barge-in / error-auth scenarios and fails loudly if any stage or artifact is missing. `--target=real` boots the REAL server code (real jwt/consent/session/registry/metering/reframer/adapters; only the socket transport is a documented node shim in place of Workers `WebSocketPair`).

### Flag
`VOICE_REALTIME_WS_ENABLED` (default off) is consumed at the WS route: mint returns 503 `voice_realtime_disabled` when off; the evidence run exercises it ON. Real runtime consumer, not a dead flag.

### Live-provider evidence (run against the REAL server, this branch)
Evidence pack (WS transcript with tokens redacted, input/output WAVs, both-side logs, stage timings, domain rows, SHA-256 index, MP4): `evidence/voice-e2e/2026-07-10T15-37-44-748Z-real-server/` (artifacts attached below; full pack retained outside repo, hashes in the index).

| scenario | result |
| --- | --- |
| baseline (real speech in -> transcript -> LLM -> real audio out) | PASS |
| barge-in (interrupt mid-speech) | PASS, **0 post-interrupt downlink frames** |
| error-auth (bad provider key) | PASS, typed `stt_transport_error`, no ready, no audio |

Measured stage deltas (baseline, live providers, monotonic clock; missing stages report `not_reached`, never zero):
- mint -> ready: **10.5ms**
- stt_final -> llm_first_text: 834ms
- llm_first_text -> tts_first_frame: 1273ms
- **stt_final -> tts_first_frame: 2107ms** (see "Latency" below)
- transcript verbatim: "What is the weather like in Denver today?"; 1.8MB real Cartesia audio captured.

### Real bugs found ONLY by the live boot (fixed in this branch, with regression tests)
1. `end_audio` advisory frame was treated as fatal `control_unknown_type` and killed the turn.
2. Empty-transcript finalization sent Cartesia a live 400 ("No valid transcripts passed") -> tts_error, zero audio. Finalization now holds one phrase back so the terminal phrase closes the context with `continue:false`.
3. Harness `stop()` hung on half-open sockets under bun canary drain-exit.
4. Harness error-auth gate accepted only one error shape; the real adapter emits `transport_error`.

### Latency (honest)
2107ms stt_final -> first audio frame is above our 1.2s target. The measured split shows two roughly equal legs (LLM first-token 834ms, TTS first-byte 1273ms). Optimization is scoped as immediate follow-up on this same evidence rig (candidates: eager-EOT speculative LLM start, TTS warm-context reuse, first-phrase fast-path). The rig measures every run, so improvements land with numbers, not adjectives.

### Tests
124 green under bun canary (CI's bun): 31 cloud-api session, 33 cloud-shared voice-session, 60 ui client. Full WS lifecycle, barge-in zero-post-cancel, revoke <=500ms, JWT expiry/revocation/claim-mismatch, metering enforcement, hello-first, malformed/oversized frames, PCM golden vectors, playback ordering, visibility-suspend.

## Fixes found along the way

- **Bench server picked node 18:** the orchestrator prepends `sys.executable`'s dir (`/usr/bin`) to PATH, shadowing modern node with system v18 (no global `crypto`) — every runtime request died with `crypto is not defined` (uuid v14). `_resolve_node()` now picks the first PATH node ≥ 20.

**1. The floating boot pill is gone entirely.** `BootStatusIndicator` ("Waking …" / "… is taking longer than usual to wake") and its grace/escalation timers are deleted from `ContinuousChatOverlay`. Boot state has no surface above the chat.

**2. The floating `CloudHandoffBanner` toast is gone too.** The shared→dedicated handoff keeps its durable home-grid tile (`agent-provisioning`), and failures now speak in the transcript (below).

**3. Boot trouble is an agent chat message with buttons.** New headless `use-boot-recovery-conductor` (mirrors the existing model-status conductor): when a boot stalls past 90 s or a dedicated-agent handoff fails/times out, it seeds ONE assistant turn (`boot:recovery`) into the live transcript with a **specific** diagnosis and remedy:
   - Eliza Cloud session unusable → *"…your Eliza Cloud session looks signed out."* → **Re-log in** (drives `handleCloudLogin`) + Try again
   - session fine, agent unresponsive → **Try again** (drives `triggerRestart`) + Re-log in
   - handoff failed/timed out → *"I couldn't finish setting up your dedicated agent…"* → **Retry setup** (re-dispatches the handoff supervisor)
   - missing local model was already covered in-chat by the model-status conductor (**Download now** / **Use Eliza Cloud instead**) — unchanged.
   Controls ride a reserved `__boot_recovery__:` value prefix consumed by the send funnel (never reaches the server); the card updates in place, returns its controls after an action settles (no dead-end "Reconnecting…" states), removes itself the moment the agent is healthy, and never renders during onboarding (first-run conductor owns that screen) or the no-provider state (the transcript's no-provider gate owns it).

**4. No chat suggestions anywhere.** The FTU welcome dashboard widget (greeting + "try saying…" chips), the resting composer suggestion strip, `usePromptSuggestions`, and the now-consumerless `POST /api/suggestions` server route are all deleted. The agent is proactive; canned prompts are gone.

**5. Onboarding is truly full-screen, then settles to half.** The content-sizing seam that shrank the pinned onboarding sheet is removed — onboarding owns the whole screen. On the completion edge the sheet **springs FULL → HALF** (was: collapse) in step with the opaque-backdrop fade, so the home appears behind the top half while the conversation stays in hand.

**6. Cloud-only onboarding confirmed unchanged** — the runtime chooser stays default-off everywhere (`first-run-runtime-flag.ts`), sign-in to Eliza Cloud is the single path.

## Tests
- NEW `use-boot-recovery-conductor.test.ts` — 11 cases: stall threshold, signed-out vs unresponsive ordering, onboarding/no-provider gating, removal on recovery, handoff card + retry dispatch, re-login/restart control flows incl. failure cards, reserved-prefix consumption.
- `ContinuousChatOverlay.test.tsx` — no-pill-ever + no-suggestions-ever regression tests replace the old banner grace-gate suite.
- `cloud-agent-lifecycle.spec.ts` — handoff test reworked to the real surfaces: home tile tracks migrating→switched; failure asserts the in-chat card and clicks `choice-__boot_recovery__:retry-handoff`.

b0:T102a,## What & why

Follow-up to **#11789** (real-model LifeOps/PA benchmark score history), closed via **#12045**. That PR ran the LifeOpsBench **Hermes** adapter against local eliza-1 models and scored **0.000 — a confound, not capability**: the gemma-4 models emit correct tools+args in gemma-native `tool_code` syntax that the Hermes XML adapter can't parse, so `agent_actions` came back empty. Its closing comment named the open residual (tracked under parent **#10721**): *"a clean capability number needs either the native `eliza` adapter on a GPU-recovered host, or teaching the Hermes adapter to parse gemma-native tool calls."*

This PR delivers that clean number via a **third path that needs neither** — the LifeOpsBench **`cerebras-direct`** agent (native OpenAI function-calling) on **Cerebras `gemma-4-31b`**, `--mode static` (deterministic `state_hash` scoring — no judge, no mock), **120 scenarios across all 10 domains**.

### Result — pass@1 **13.3% (16/120)**, mean score 0.245

calendar 50% · mail 25% · travel 25% · reminders 17% · finance 8% · focus 8% · contacts/messages/health/sleep 0%.

Crucially, **`agent_actions` is populated and executed on every domain** (`CALENDAR_CREATE_EVENT`, `MESSAGE_SEND`, `ENTITY`, `HEALTH`, …) — **no parse artifact**, unlike #12045's empty-actions confound. The 0.000s are *genuine* failure modes (hand-reviewed): partial world state (0.3 near-misses), correct state but wrong answer text, and read-loops hitting `max_turns`. So this is a real capability signal: gemma-4-31b is strong on single-shot writes, weak on multi-step read-summarize-and-answer.

### Also operationalizes the retention decision #12045 made in prose

- **`score-history.jsonl` + `HISTORY.md`** — an append-only, harness-keyed series seeded with every real-model point to date: TS prompt-benchmark `gpt-oss-120b` 70% (#12022), local eliza-1 0.0% confounded (#12045), and this `cerebras-direct` 13.3% clean. Regenerated from the jsonl; never hand-edited.
- **`scripts/append-score-history.mjs`** — zero-dep appender ingesting either report format (`--report` or `--report-dir`).
- **`.github/workflows/lifeops-benchmark-history.yml`** — the nightly lane #12045's README named, **opt-in and inert on merge**: no-ops without a `CEREBRAS_API_KEY` secret, `schedule:` commented out. A maintainer enables it with the secret + cron.

- **Real-LLM trajectories:** raw per-domain JSON (`lifeops_gemma-4-31b_<domain>.json`) with the full model I/O per turn — `agent_actions`, `agent_message`, tokens, latency, `total_score`, `state_hash_match` (the deterministic `tool_results` world observations are elided for size, reproducible via the run command; 356KB total); a hand-reviewed `scorecard.md`; `scorecard.sample-trajectories.json` (one pass + one fail); machine `scorecard.summary.json`. # Summary

- Add a first-party Authorization Code + PKCE lifecycle for the fixed `ai.elizaos.app` client and exact `https://eliza.app/auth/callback` redirect.
- Mint a short-lived hash-only authorization code, create one inactive encrypted credential on exchange, and activate it transactionally only after the native client proves durable Keychain receipt.
- Add crash/retry-safe exchange, acknowledgement, self-revocation, signed-in account recovery, expiry cleanup, app-deactivation revocation, and additive database migrations.
- Keep mobile credentials primary-consistent and outside positive auth caches; prevent them from managing generic credentials or delegated access.
- Apply route-isolated admission/ingress limits and reject mobile credentials in WebSocket query strings. Ordinary Cloud/browser WebSocket tokens retain their existing behavior.
- Regenerate the canonical Hono router and public SDK wrappers.

# Rollout and compatibility

- The feature fails closed unless `ELIZA_MOBILE_APP_AUTH_ENABLED` is exactly `true`, the environment is exactly `staging` or `production`, and `ELIZA_MOBILE_APP_AUTH_APP_ID` is a live approved app UUID whose allowed origins include the fixed callback.
- Neither flag is configured by this PR. No staging or production deployment/enablement was performed from this branch.
- Migrations are additive. Existing API keys, sessions, browser auth, Android, desktop, local, and remote-host flows retain their existing contracts.
- Mobile credentials use headers only. The server returns `mobile_credential_transport_forbidden` for `eliza_mobile_*` URL query tokens so a long-lived secret is never forwarded through the generic WebSocket channel.
- The credential is finite-lived (30 days), attributable to the configured app, individually recoverable/revocable, and tombstoned with encrypted reveal material erased.

## Executive Summary
In July 2026, the ElizaOS project focused on transforming the framework into a production-ready ecosystem by hardening security, improving financial reliability, and expanding agent capabilities. These efforts ensure that our AI agents are not only more intelligent and versatile but also operate within a secure, stable, and commercially viable infrastructure.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Building a Secure and Reliable Foundation**
_Goal: We aimed to make the platform safer for commercial use and more dependable for developers by removing technical debt and strengthening security._
- We implemented robust financial safeguards and secure payment systems to support monetization ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/10942), [#11606](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11606)).
- We hardened our security by protecting sensitive model credentials and creating safer, isolated environments for agent operations ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11660), [#11402](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11402)).
- We established strict error-handling policies to replace silent failures with clear, actionable reporting, significantly improving system reliability ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/13236)).

**Advancing Agent Intelligence and Versatility**
_Goal: We wanted to make our agents smarter and more capable of handling complex, real-world scenarios._
- We expanded the LifeOps framework with over 240 new persona scenarios, allowing agents to act more naturally in diverse situations ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12356)).
- We upgraded our core intelligence by adopting the latest Gemma-4 benchmarks and creating a new pipeline to train smaller, more efficient models ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11196), [#11891](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11891)).

**Improving User Accessibility and Experience**
_Goal: We focused on making the ElizaOS experience seamless across mobile and desktop devices._
- We introduced voice-first features for mobile users, including keyboard extensions and live activity tracking for voice sessions ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12685), [#12503](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12503)).
- We modernized the desktop experience with faster communication tools and a more visually appealing command-line interface ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/12485), [#11591](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/11591)).

## Problem

`app-live-e2e.yml` is the only scheduled CI home for the packaged Electrobun desktop suite (`xvfb-run … bun run --cwd packages/app test:desktop:packaged`, line 380) — and it has failed every night for at least three consecutive nights (Jul 1, Jul 2, Jul 3 2026). In the latest completed run **all four jobs failed** (desktop packaged, app live chat, full walkthrough, cloud login+provision+chat). A nightly that is always red is indistinguishable from no lane: nobody is alerted, regressions accumulate silently, and the desktop loop has no unattended green cadence at all.

Desktop-job specifics from run 28647271527 (2026-07-03):

1. `desktop-launch-render.e2e.spec.ts:110` — bridge screenshot 503; the ubuntu runner has none of `scrot`/`import`/`ffmpeg`/`xwd` installed (workflow installs protobuf but no screenshot tool).

3. Lane summary: 2 failed / 2 skipped / 1 passed — most of the suite is macOS-gated, so the Linux leg exercises very little even when green.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)c1:T1005,## Context

Green CI does not mean the change is tested. Two layers fail open.

### Coverage enforcement is advisory (re-opens the core of closed #9943/#8801)

- `lint-lane-coverage.mjs` runs `--dry-run` warn-only (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml:150-154`) and `ci.yaml` triggers on `[main]` only (`:9-12`), so it doesn't even run on develop PRs. Live state: **160 blocking issues, 104/146 plugins missing deterministic E2E/scenario coverage**, all suppressed by `--dry-run`; `lint-lane-coverage.allowlist.json` doesn't exist.
- `coverage-gate.yml` is the only per-change coverage gate and is structurally narrow: it runs only when a **changed test file** exists (`:6-8`,`:88-91`) — a PR adding new source with no test never appears in lcov, so nothing fails; it **skips any test importing vitest** (`:61-64`), and ~4,401 test files import vitest vs ~1,291 `bun:test`, so it covers a minority; threshold is a 50% ratchet.

Net: **nothing requires new code to ship real tests.**

### Vacuous-green holes on the PR hot path

- The runner's `--min-tasks`/`MIN_TEST_TASKS` floors (`packages/scripts/run-all-tests.mjs:256-266,1138,1190`) default to `0` and are set by **no** PR lane (`test`, `test:server`, `test:client`, `test:plugins`, `test:e2e`). So a lane whose tasks all self-skip ("No test files found") exits **green**. The only floor enforcement, `ci-full-matrix-proof.mjs`, uses `--plan=json` (static discovery, never executes tests) and runs twice-daily/narrow-path (`ci-full-matrix-proof.yml:17-32`), off the PR path.
- **`outputIndicatesNoTests` swallows real failures.** `run-all-tests.mjs:359-366` + `:969-972`: any **non-zero** child exit is reclassified as `skipped:true` (→ green) if the last 16 KB of merged stdout+stderr matches `/No test files found/i` / `/did not match any test files/i`. A multi-project vitest / `bun test` run where one project legitimately has no files while another **fails** produces both strings in one buffer → the whole task is marked SKIP=green, hiding the failure. Same pattern in the cloud step (`:1030-1035`).

> The iOS/Android-sim manifestations of this are tracked device-specifically in sibling umbrella #13562 (#13571 "boot-to-error-card passes, whole runs go green with 0 passed", #13572 "test:sim:local-chat passes vacuously when no simulator"). This issue fixes the **general runner mechanism** those lanes rely on.

## Tasks

- [ ] Seed `lint-lane-coverage.allowlist.json` from today's 160 issues (loader already supports it); flip the gate off `--dry-run`; add it to a develop-triggered workflow (`quality.yml`).
- [ ] Extend `coverage-gate.yml` to require a covering test for changed source, and to include vitest tests (or add a vitest coverage lane).
- [ ] Set `MIN_TEST_TASKS`/`--min-tasks` on the real PR lanes (`test`, `test:server`, `test:client`, `test:plugins`, `test:e2e`) with realistic floors.
- [ ] Narrow the "no tests" classification to the runner's own empty-file determination (or an exact-banner match on the whole output), not a substring scan over merged child output.

## Acceptance criteria

- A new surface-bearing plugin with no scenario **reds** on a develop PR; a PR adding untested source **reds**.
- A lane filtered to zero tasks exits **3**, not 0 (extend `run-all-tests-vacuous-green-guard.test.ts`).
- A suite with an empty sub-project **and** a failing test **FAILS** (does not SKIP=green).

## Files

`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`, `quality.yml`, `coverage-gate.yml`, `packages/scripts/run-all-tests.mjs`, `packages/scripts/lint-lane-coverage.mjs` (+ new allowlist), `packages/scripts/__tests__/run-all-tests-vacuous-green-guard.test.ts`.

Worse, most legs are signal-only (`|| true`), so even a dispatched run only hard-gates onboarding→home + native-plugin-view: the route sweep, touch-gesture matrix, view-runtime soak, launcher gesture loop, and the on-device local chat smoke can all regress without turning anything red. ## Current state
- Storage: transcripts = memories rows, `tableName 'transcripts'`, `content.transcript` JSON (`transcript-store.ts:24-27`); `plugin-meetings` writer byte-compatible (golden test).
- Contract: `packages/shared/src/transcripts.ts` — `TranscriptScope:51-56`; consent/policy/permission vocabularies (`TRANSCRIPT_CONSENT_STATES:110-118` etc.) exist but are UNWIRED (grep-clean in plugin-meetings).
- Redaction primitives: `redact.ts`, `secret-swap.ts`, `pii-pseudonymizer.ts` + `entity-recognizer.ts` (`packages/core/src/security/`); export-variant precedent `TrajectoriesService.redactTrajectoryPrompts` (`TrajectoriesService.ts:2528-2537`).
- Roster: `MeetingSession.participants` (`packages/shared/src/meetings.ts:101-114`).

## Proposed change
1. Agent actions (roleGated via `satisfiesRoleGate`, AccessContext-checked via `hasRoleAccess` `roles.ts:979`):
   - `REDACT_TRANSCRIPT` (minRole USER on own scope, ADMIN for others'): generates a redacted VARIANT — pipeline over segments+text: detectPii + entity recognizers + PseudonymSession (deterministic per transcript); variant stored as new transcript-linked record + (if exported) new media object with new sha256; original untouched; redacted DTO **withholds audioUrl** (audio never redacted in v1).
   - `SHARE_TRANSCRIPT` (grant per PERM-ACL: person or room-snapshot; mode full|redacted).
   - **Admin ask→redact-for-all**: ADMIN in the meeting room asks the agent → redacted variant becomes the disclosed version for every non-privileged grant; OWNER/ADMIN retain full.
2. Persist consent state at capture (`TRANSCRIPT_CONSENT_STATES` recorded from the meeting flow) — storage only; enforcement out of scope.
3. Wire the marker retirement path: share/download/delete unified with the Files surface per #8876 AD-completeness(2) (`TRANSCRIPT_MARKER` round-trip at `TranscriptViewerOverlay.tsx:54` slated for retirement) — do the transcript-share part here, full unification tracked in #8876 follow-ups.

## Acceptance criteria
- Live-LLM scenario: meeting transcript captured → participant asks agent to share → agent shares redacted to USER, full to ADMIN — trajectory evidence attached and read.
- Variant determinism test (same transcript → same surrogates); original + chat copy + audio byte-identical after redaction.
- Actions respect roleGate; denied attempts audit-logged.

## Out of scope
Audio waveform redaction, consent ENFORCEMENT, UI (PERM-UX).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)c6:Ta40,## The layer under #15205
With the CF wildcard + TLS fixed (#15205), the app's per-agent calls now correctly reach `https://<id>.staging.elizacloud.ai` on the STAGING worker (verified: valid `*.staging.elizacloud.ai` cert, request lands on the staging cloud-api worker, no longer the prod one). But the chat still dead-ends: every `/api/*` call returns **HTTP 404 from Cloudflare with no CORS header** → browser reports `No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin'`.

## Root cause (systemic, not per-agent)
The worker's `handleDedicatedAgentProxy` → `proxyToOrigin` forwards to `AGENT_ROUTER_ORIGIN_HOST = eliza-staging-1.elizacloud.ai` (the staging CP). The CP runs **nginx** (:80/:443) which routes `<id>.staging.elizacloud.ai` to the agent over the **headscale tailnet** via the agent's `headscale_ip`. But:
- **All 48 running staging agents have `headscale_ip` NULL/empty** (`SELECT (headscale_ip IS NULL OR headscale_ip='') , count(*) FROM agent_sandboxes WHERE status='running'` → `t | 48`).
- **`headscale nodes list` on the CP shows NO online agent-tagged node** — only `cp-staging-router` (tag:eliza-proxy, online) and two `robot-tstest`/`robot-tstest2` (tag:agent) **offline since 2026-06-16**.

So staging agent containers are provisioned + running + serving on their node bridge (`bridge_url` is set, e.g. `http://91.98.38.74:19006`), but they **never join the headscale mesh**, so the CP router has no tailnet address to reach them → 404. The agent's own CORS (`resolveCorsOrigin`, which allows any origin when `ELIZA_CLOUD_PROVISIONED=1`) is never reached because the request dies at the CP hop.

## Why it surfaced only now
Nobody ever got a staging agent reachable end-to-end before tonight (DB split #15160 → image boot #15196 → wildcard/TLS #15205 all had to land first). This is the next distinct gap in the same 'staging never fully mirrored prod' class, adjacent to the known prod-parity headscale gap.

## What to investigate
Why staging agent containers don't join headscale: is the tailscale-up / headscale pre-auth-key step injected at provision time (the staging worker HAS `HEADSCALE_PUBLIC_URL`/`HEADSCALE_API_URL`/`HEADSCALE_USER=tunnel`) actually running in the container, and is the provisioning worker recording `headscale_ip` back to `agent_sandboxes`? Either the join is failing/skipped or the IP is never persisted. Fixing it should light up all 48 agents at once.

## Scope
Systemic (48/48 agents), needs the headscale/tailnet provisioning path debugged — an infra workstream, not a config toggle. #15205's edge routing is done and verified; this is the CP→agent hop. [stan-cloud]c7:Tc14,## Project / Coordination

[filed by stan-cloud on behalf of @standujar]ce:T1851,Part of the corpus PII scrub pipeline (multimodal foundation) — and a standalone knowledge-hub improvement.

## Problem

Transcripts already mirror into knowledge and are chunked/embedded like documents, but the mirror is `transcriptPlainText()` (`packages/shared/src/transcripts.ts`), which STRIPS all timing; fragments inherit `transcriptId`/`audioUrl` but have no per-fragment time range. Consequences:

- A search hit cannot seek the stored audio — the player opens at t=0.
- The PII pipeline cannot map a text-PII span found in a fragment back to an audio timestamp span, which `[pii] Audio redaction` requires.
- **Live data-loss bug (prerequisite):** voice-session WAVs are invisible to the media GC. `transcriptKnowledgePayload` sets ONLY `metadata.audioUrl` (`plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/transcript-knowledge.ts:66`) while `collectReferencedMedia` scans only `content.attachments[].url`/`thumbnailUrl` + `metadata.mediaUrl` (`packages/agent/src/api/media-runtime.ts:161-193`), so the WAV is swept after the 1h grace on the next daily `MEDIA_GC`. `meeting-transcript-writer.ts:425-432` documents this exact hazard and sets BOTH keys; the voice-session path does not. Timestamps into deleted audio are meaningless.

Producer fidelity today: local fused eliza-1-asr ABI v12 gives per-word ms spans (`asrTranscribeTimed`, `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/ffi-bindings.ts:395/918/2193`); meeting segments carry `words: []` because the seam is the locked string-only `ModelType.TRANSCRIPTION` (`plugins/plugin-meetings/src/pipeline/transcriber.ts` header documents why); the cloud STT route parses only `{text}` and discards all timestamps (`packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/stt/route.ts`).

## Architecture

1. **Pre-chunked ingest seam:** optional `fragments?: Array<{text, metadata: {segmentIds, startMs, endMs, speakerLabels}}>` input on `DocumentService.addDocument` (`packages/core/src/features/documents/service.ts:645`) / `processFragmentsSynchronously` (`packages/core/src/features/documents/document-processor.ts:95`). `fragmentMetadata` already spreads document metadata, so per-fragment `startMs`/`endMs` rides jsonb metadata — zero schema/table change.
2. **Producers chunk on segment boundaries:** `transcriptKnowledgePayload` (`plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/transcript-knowledge.ts`) and `plugins/plugin-meetings/src/transcripts/meeting-transcript-writer.ts` build ~chunk-size groups from `Transcript.segments` they already hold — never splitting inside a segment.
3. **Project anchors through search:** `/api/documents/search` result mapping (`plugins/plugin-documents/src/routes.ts:785`) adds `transcriptId`, `startMs`, `endMs` next to `documentId`/`position`; same for the `documents` action=search formatter (`packages/core/src/features/documents/actions.ts`) so agent-facing hits carry anchors.
4. **Deep-link playback:** `packages/ui/src/components/pages/documents-detail.tsx` / TranscriptPlayer accept an initial seek (`?t=<ms>` or prop); `flattenTranscriptWords`/`activeWordIndex` already exist — only the entry offset is missing.
5. **GC fix (prerequisite):** set `metadata.mediaUrl = audioUrl` in `transcriptKnowledgePayload` (matching the meeting writer) AND/OR make `collectReferencedMedia` also collect `metadata.audioUrl`.
6. **Producer fidelity (second priority within this issue):**
   - Meetings word timings: expose timed ASR as a real runtime seam — a service or additive typed model registration in plugin-local-inference wrapping `transcribePcmTimed`/`asrTranscribeTimed` — so plugin-meetings' `AsrBackend` can return `words[]` when the fused v12 lib serves. Do NOT widen the locked `ModelType.TRANSCRIPTION` ⇒ string contract; add a parallel typed surface.
   - Cloud STT timestamps: `packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/stt/route.ts` requests `response_format=verbose_json` (+ `timestamp_granularities` where the deployed faster-whisper supports it), parses segments/words, and returns them in the DTO alongside `transcript`.
7. **Edits stay correct for free:** `TranscriptService.update` already deletes + re-adds the mirror; segment-boundary chunking re-derives anchors from patched segments.
8. **Documented caveat, not fixed here:** v12 word timings are duration-proportional char-weighted, not forced alignment — sufficient for seek/highlight anchors; `validateAsrWordTimings` (`packages/shared/src/transcripts.ts`) remains the producer gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fragment rows for a mirrored transcript carry `startMs`/`endMs`/`segmentIds`; boundaries never split a segment (unit + integration against real fixture audio — `plugins/plugin-local-inference/native/audio-fixtures/freeman.wav`, harness pattern `asr-timed.real.test.ts`).
- `/api/documents/search` and the `documents` action return `transcriptId` + `startMs` + `endMs`; UI evidence: MP4 walkthrough — search a word, click the hit, the player opens mid-audio at the anchor and the word is audible.
- **GC regression test:** seeded voice-session transcript + WAV → run the referenced-set computation → WAV survives; the test FAILS on current develop behavior.
- Meetings: with the fused v12 lib present, meeting segments carry `words[]` (`*.real.test.ts` lane, skipped-never-faked when the lib/bundle is absent); cloud STT DTO carries segments/words (live contract test precedent: `packages/cloud/api/__tests__/voice-kokoro-whisper-live.test.ts`).
- Transcript edit → re-mirror recomputes anchors (test patches a segment, asserts new fragment ranges).
- Evidence inline in the PR: fragment row dumps, search JSON, deep-link playback video, GC logs (`PR_EVIDENCE.md`).

## Out of scope

The PII scrub itself; audio muting (`[pii] Audio redaction`); any second file store or files/refcount table (#8876); whisper.cpp resurrection (retired — fused eliza-1-asr only); widening `ModelType.TRANSCRIPTION`.

## Pipeline integration

This is the multimodal pipeline's text↔time bridge: the LLM-pass finds PII in fragment text; fragment anchors + word timings convert verdicts to timestamp spans consumed by `[pii] Audio redaction`. Fragments are documents, so the corpus enumeration and `pii:<sha256>:v<ruleset>` idempotency layers apply unchanged.
cf:T1200,## Summary

A live production audit of the provisioning pipeline (2026-07-29) found **agent deletion is failing 100% of the time**, and has been for days. This is customer-visible and accelerating.

Over the last 7 days: **554 failed jobs vs 153 completed** (78% failure rate).

## 1. `agent_delete` is completely broken — 160/160 failures, one identical cause

Every failed `agent_delete` job in the window carries the same error:

```
value.toISOString is not a function
```

- 160 failures, all identical, most recent **2026-07-28 18:03 UTC** (still current).
- All of them exhausted `attempts >= max_attempts` — so each one also burned the full retry budget.
- Consequence: **37 agents are stuck in `deletion_failed`**, up from 5 five days ago, and accelerating: **17 of them in the last 24 hours alone**.
- Customers who ask to delete an agent get a failure, the agent stays, and it keeps occupying node capacity.

`value.toISOString is not a function` is Drizzle's timestamp serializer receiving a **string where a `Date` is expected** — the same class as the cache/JSON round-trip defect fixed in #16859/#16860 for `resolveSharedAgent`.

One concrete candidate worth checking first (not yet proven to be the site): `prepareAgentBackupInsertData` (`packages/cloud/shared/src/db/repositories/agent-sandboxes.ts`) does

```ts
const createdAt = data.created_at ?? new Date();
// ...
created_at: createdAt,
```

`??` only guards `null`/`undefined` — a value that already crossed a JSON boundary as an ISO **string** passes straight through into the timestamp column. The 4 non-restart `agent_snapshot` failures in the same window are literally `Failed query: insert into "agent_sandbox_backups" (...)`, which is that insert.

## 2. `agent_snapshot`: 386 failures, 381 of them not the job's fault

```
Job interrupted by worker restart 2 times - max attempts reached   (381)
Failed query: insert into "agent_sandbox_backups" ...              (4)
Job timed out 2 times - max attempts reached                       (1)
```

The worker keeps restarting mid-snapshot, and **each restart consumes an attempt**. Two restarts exhaust `max_attempts` and the job is marked permanently failed — even though nothing about the job itself failed. A restart is an infrastructure event, not a job defect, and should not spend the job's retry budget (the codebase already has the shape for this: `retryLaterWithoutIncrementingAttempts`).

Why the worker restarts so often is the second half of this: it is consistent with the heap abort in #17154 and with the unbounded source-side snapshot capture in #17172 §1 (a large agent's capture is materialized entirely in the worker's heap).

## 3. The fleet is at or over capacity

| node | capacity | running |
|---|---|---|
| eliza-core-prod-2 | 24 | 24 |
| eliza-core-prod-3 | 24 | **25** |
| eliza-core-prod-4 | 24 | 24 |
| eliza-core-prod-5 | 24 | 24 |
| eliza-core-prod-6 | 24 | 24 |

prod-3 is **over** its declared capacity, and every robot is full, so new work is spilling onto autoscaled cloud nodes (3 × 4 running). Note the interaction: the 37 undeletable agents and the 45 in `error` are holding slots that should have been reclaimed — the delete failure is directly feeding the capacity pressure.

Also present: a `knowledge_processing` job stuck `in_progress` since **2025-12-31** (~7 months), which no sweeper has reclaimed.

## Why these compound

The three interact rather than being independent:
1. Deletes fail → agents accumulate (`deletion_failed` 37, `error` 45) → capacity fills.
2. Snapshots fail on worker restart → upgrades/deletes that depend on a restore point are less safe.
3. Full capacity → more scheduling pressure → longer boots → more exposure to the sweeper/timeout classes (#17215).

## Asks

- [ ] Pin and fix the `toISOString` write in the delete path — deterministic, 100% reproducible, highest customer impact.
- [ ] A worker restart must not consume a job's retry budget (`retryLaterWithoutIncrementingAttempts` semantics for interruption).
- [ ] Recover the 37 `deletion_failed` + 45 `error` rows once the above land (see #17162 for the 44-agent precedent and its recovery constraints).
- [ ] Reconcile declared capacity vs actual (prod-3 at 25/24), and reclaim the 7-month-stuck `in_progress` job.

Evidence gathered live against production (counts, error strings, timings; no customer identifiers). Related: #17215 (sweeper vs in-flight cold boots), #17154 (worker heap abort), #17172 (snapshot budgets), #17162 (the 2026-07-13 stranding), #17185 (delete must release capacity exactly once). _Workstream: **Voice pipeline** · [design doc](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/develop/packages/docs/ongoing-development/research/07-voice-pipeline.md) · [MVP board](https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/projects/15)_d2:T2335,## Light Phone III voice pipeline — findings, fixes, and remaining work (cloud STT/TTS on stripped AOSP)

Tracking issue for the LP3 (Light Phone III) hybrid-cloud voice work. The LP3 is a 6 GB, Qualcomm Adreno 613, **stripped LightOS/AOSP** device: no Google speech-recognition service, no proprietary media codecs in the WebView, and it runs the on-device agent over a Unix socket rather than a TCP port. Those three gaps break every native voice assumption in the app, and each surfaced as a separate bug. This documents what we found, what we fixed, the architecture, and what's still open.

**Mode:** hybrid — the on-device agent runtime boots locally, but text inference is **direct Cerebras** (`gemma-4-31b`, OPENAI-compat passthrough), and voice is routed to **Eliza Cloud** (STT/TTS). Local on-device voice (Shaw's Kokoro + fused Gemma ASR) works but is ~10–16 s/turn on this CPU, so cloud is the pragmatic path.

---

### ✅ What works now
- **Text chat** — Cerebras `gemma-4-31b`, ~2–3 s, streams tokens (SSE).
- **Cloud STT** — `POST /api/asr/cloud` → Eliza Cloud **OpenAI Whisper**, ~1.8–2.4 s, accurate transcripts.
- **Mic capture** — the waveform/"talk" button now records via the WebView (getUserMedia) on the cloud path; **no native recognizer, no loop** (verified: 0 `Recognition error (5)`, mic `curActiveCount=1`).
- **Cloud TTS fetch** — `POST /api/tts/cloud` → 200, MP3 audio, ~2–2.8 s.
- **End-to-end pipeline fires**: speech → transcript → Gemma reply → TTS fetch. Confirmed live (agent replied "not much, just here and ready to help").

### ❌ The one remaining blocker: audio playback (no MP3 codec)
The cloud returns **MP3** (`audio/mpeg`, ElevenLabs `eleven_flash_v2_5`). LightOS's WebView **cannot decode MP3 by any path**:
- `AudioContext.decodeAudioData(mp3)` → throws `Unable to decode audio data`.
- `<audio>` element with an MP3 blob → `MediaError code 4` (SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED).

So the reply is generated correctly but is **silent**. This is the single thing standing between "works" and "works with sound."

**Fix options (ranked):**
1. **Make the cloud TTS return WAV/PCM** for this client — WAV needs no codec and `decodeAudioData` handles it. There is currently **no `outputFormat`/`format` param** on `/voice/tts` (verified), so this needs a cloud-side option (or a Kokoro-cloud path that emits WAV). *Recommended.*
2. Ship a **WASM MP3 decoder** in the client for codec-less WebViews (heavier bundle).
3. Use **local Kokoro TTS** (returns WAV) — but it's slow on LP3 and the native voice lib got dropped in the APK rebuild (see below).

---

### 🐞 Bugs found + fixes (the saga)
Each of these was a distinct LP3-specific failure. Commits are local (not pushed).

1. **On-device agent chat-send 404** — the Android local-agent IPC bridge only served *plugin* routes (`runtime.routes`); core routes (`/api/conversations`, message stream, etc.) 404'd. Fixed by bridging the full server request handler through the IPC path. *(iOS/HTTP parity bug — genuinely upstream-worthy.)*

2. **On-device CPU voice via the bionic host** — the fused `libelizainference` can't be dlopen'd by the musl agent; runs in-app via JNI over a UDS. Vulkan backend **SIGSEGVs on Adreno 613** (Mali-only), so added an opt-in **CPU** path (`eliza:voice-cpu-host`). Proven: local Kokoro TTS 200/audio, fused ASR real transcript. KEY: `eliza_inference_create` is metadata-only — **voice never loads the 1.27 GB text model** (Shaw's lazy design). *Slow (~16 s) but works.*

3. **Native mic → infinite recognizer loop** — the app registers **itself** as the Android `RecognitionService`. On LP3 (no real recognizer), a native STT attempt hits `ElizaRecognitionService.onStartListening` → fires the `elizaos://voice` deep-link → `toggleHandsFree` → `startListening` → native again → **infinite loop** (`Recognition error: Client error (5)` every ~0.6 s). Broken by routing capture entirely to cloud (below).

4. **THE root cause — capture factory ignored the cloud preference** — `resolveBackendKind` (`voice-capture-factory.ts`) returned `"talkmode"` for **any** native platform **before** it ever checked `preferred === "eliza-cloud"`. So the hands-free capture (`useShellController.startCapture` → `createVoiceCapture`, a path entirely separate from `useVoiceChat.startListening`) **always** used the native recognizer and ignored the cloud setting. Fixed: an explicit `eliza-cloud`/`openai` ASR preference now wins over native talk-mode when WAV capture exists (undefined/local-inference still prefer native → other devices unchanged).

5. **Opt-in cloud voice plumbing** (`eliza:voice-cloud-tts`) — forces `cloudConnected`/`asrProvider` to cloud since the hybrid config never advertises cloud voice (`/api/cloud/status` returns `cloudVoiceProxyAvailable:false` because `serviceRouting.tts` isn't `cloud-proxy`). Read via the **live Capacitor bridge** (`Capacitor.Plugins.Preferences`), because `import("@capacitor/preferences")` can resolve to a web-stub that silently returns nothing (this is why the opt-in didn't arm the first time).

6. **Text brain → Cerebras Gemma** — swapped `gpt-oss-120b` → `gemma-4-31b` (matches the dedicated cloud agent). Verified live.

7. **MP3 playback** — added an `<audio>`-element fallback for `decodeAudioData` failures... which then revealed LightOS has **no MP3 codec at all** (see blocker above). Fallback is in place for WebViews that *do* have MP3 but not this one.

**Regression to note:** the APK rebuilds for the web-bundle fixes were built without the voice-lib staging flags, so the APK **dropped `libelizavoicejni.so`** → the bionic host can't start → **local on-device voice is currently broken on the shipped APK** (cloud voice unaffected). Libs are saved; restore or rebuild with the voice-lib pin to bring local voice back.

---

### 🏗️ Architecture notes (for whoever picks this up)
- **Two separate capture paths.** Composer dictate (Mic icon) → `useVoiceChat.startListening`. Hands-free "talk" (waveform) → `useShellController.startCapture` → `createVoiceCapture`. They do **not** share code — a fix in one doesn't cover the other (this cost several rounds).
- **`useShellVoiceOutput` is output-only** (TTS); it uses `useVoiceChat` but the mic is owned entirely by `startCapture`.
- **Web UI is baked into the APK** (`assets/public`, no `server.url` in `capacitor.config`) → every UI change needs `build:web` + rsync to the platform dir + `gradlew assembleDebug` + reinstall. No hot-swap.
- **Deferred boot is slow on LP3** (~2 min; vision plugin alone ~25 s). The elizacloud *routes* register at the very end of the app-route tail, so `/api/{asr,tts}/cloud` **404 transiently** right after boot — poll `agent.log` for `elizacloud:routes` before testing (not a bug).

### 🎙️ End-of-turn detection + STT (answering "is it the best?")
- **End-of-turn:** works. Two layers — an **energy VAD** (`DEFAULT_LOCAL_ASR_AUTO_STOP`: `silenceMs: 650`, RMS threshold `0.003`) ends a turn after 650 ms of silence, plus a **semantic TurnAggregator** in converse mode so a mid-clause pause doesn't cut off. It's **silence-based**, so long pauses split into multiple turns and there's ~0.65 s of trailing-silence latency.
- **STT model:** **OpenAI Whisper** via Eliza Cloud (`/voice/stt`, provider `openai`/`whisper`). Accurate and robust, but the client path is **batch** (record full utterance → upload whole clip), so **no live word-by-word transcript**.
- **Streaming reality:** text generation **streams** (Cerebras SSE) and pipelines **sentence-by-sentence** into TTS (speech starts before the full reply is done). But **STT is batch** and **TTS returns per-sentence clips** (not byte-streamed). So it is *not* fully token-streamed end-to-end.

### 🚀 What could be better / recommendations
- **Streaming STT** (Deepgram Nova-3 / streaming Whisper) → live transcript + lower latency vs record-then-upload.
- **Neural end-of-turn detection** (LiveKit turn-detector / Krisp) → semantic turn-taking instead of a fixed 650 ms silence window (no pause-splitting, snappier responses).
- **Chunked/streamed TTS audio** → start speaking a sentence before its full clip arrives.
- **WAV output from cloud TTS** → the concrete fix for the MP3-codec-less WebView (see blocker).
- **Codec capability detection** → detect no-MP3 WebViews and auto-request WAV.

### 📋 Remaining work
- [ ] Cloud TTS returns WAV (or client MP3 decoder) → **make voice audible on LP3** (top priority).
- [ ] Restore `libelizavoicejni.so` in the APK build (voice-lib staging) → local on-device voice back.
- [ ] Fix the native local TTS path (`TalkModePlugin.kt` dials dead TCP `127.0.0.1:31337`; should reach the agent's real UDS) → fully-local mic voice.
- [ ] (Optional, larger) streaming STT + neural turn detection for a conversational feel.

*All code changes this session are local commits on a working branch; nothing pushed. Secrets/tokens redacted.*
d3:Teee,## Problem

The post-merge commit `e8e604732ca532f5c32633f82b894e1f7cbe2ab9` on `chore/simplify-remove-defensive-antipatterns` tries to replace the React-mounted LifeOps activity hook with a self-starting `src/register.ts` entry. The goal is sound—activity capture should not depend on one route/component remaining mounted—but the proposed `appRegister` architecture is not safe to merge.

`packages/app` currently schedules the package-root `ui.ts` loader and generated side-effect loaders through one cache keyed only by package name. Personal Assistant would therefore use `@elizaos/plugin-personal-assistant` for both entries. Whichever loader wins suppresses the other; if `register.ts` wins, consumers expecting the blocker-card module receive the wrong namespace. The side-effect loader also runs in popout/detached/app-window renderers and discards disposers. The proposed controller is neither idempotent nor race-safe: an awaited native startup can finish after `stop()` and install a late listener/interval.

The cleanup portion of the source branch was already squash-merged in #16423. The remaining commit also reverts unrelated cleanup across roughly 70 files, so it must not be cherry-picked wholesale.

d6:T12f8,## Summary

The first `/api/v1/chat/completions` request in a fresh Cloudflare Worker isolate dynamically evaluates the entire Cloud API route graph. The current generated router statically imports **646 routes**, so chat initializes unrelated analytics, voice, payments, containers, crypto, admin, local-database, and SDK trees before it can serve one inference request.

This is the remaining cold/idle component after #16153's Railway-Redis ingress bug. Keep the fixes separate: #16153 removes deterministic network stalls from the two protective limiters; this issue makes chat stop paying the monolithic application bootstrap.

## Reproduction and measurements

Measured against cloud code matching current `develop`:

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---:|
| Full Worker bundle | 16.16 MiB raw / 3.608 MiB gzip |
| Inputs bundled | 10,574 |
| `node_modules` inputs | 7,646 / 11.77 MiB |
| Generated route modules | 643 / 1.01 MiB |
| Health before full-app initialization | 11.7 ms local |
| First unauthenticated chat after health | 1,043 ms |
| Next chat requests | 2.5–3.6 ms |
| Source import of `bootstrap-app` | 4,635 ms |
| Actual `createApp()` after imports | 13 ms |
| Chat-route-only prototype | 5.12 MiB / 1.277 MiB gzip |

The one-route prototype is about **68% smaller raw** and **65% smaller compressed**. Registration is not the bottleneck; import/module evaluation is.

Cloudflare documents that larger bundles increase startup time and recommends splitting functionality across Workers. It also documents Service Bindings as internal Worker-to-Worker calls without added network latency:

- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/bundling/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/service-bindings/

## Ranked dependency causes

1. `_router.generated.ts` statically imports and mounts the entire 646-route API.
2. Worker production bundles PGlite/local database code that it cannot use.
3. Chat-reachable service imports use the repository barrel, pulling unrelated repositories and SDKs.
4. `CacheClient` imports every backend; `randomUUID()` also currently runs at module construction, which prevents a naive static route-only Worker from starting under workerd.
5. Public chat passes global auth's allowlist immediately, but static imports still pull the full Steward/session/admin graph.
6. Off-path Nodemailer, AWS S3, ElevenLabs, ExcelJS, Solana, sandbox/runtime, and plugin trees initialize with the monolith.

## Safe implementation sequence

1. Add a feature-flagged inference entry in the thin Worker entrypoint and dispatch only the exact canonical/compatibility inference paths before `getApp()`.
2. Preserve the existing request shell: Cloud/DB/R2 contexts, request ID, CORS, security/no-store headers, structured observation, error mapping, auth, rate limiting, billing, streaming, aborts, and deferred settlement.
3. Move protected-only auth/audit imports behind their branch, use direct repository imports, make `CacheClient.instanceId` request-lazy, and remove/stub Worker-inapplicable dependencies from this entry.
4. If parsing remains material, deploy an internal `eliza-cloud-inference-{staging,prod}` Worker behind a Service Binding. Deploy target first, caller/binding second, and retain a one-flag fallback through soak.

Do not merge a naive static chat-route entry: the current global-scope `randomUUID()` fails Worker startup and must be made request-lazy first.

## Required parity proof

- CI dry-run plus bundle metafile; initial inference target no larger than 1.5 MiB gzip.
- Fresh-workerd health → cold unauth chat → warm chat benchmark.
- Golden old/new comparisons for API-key, bearer, cookie, wallet, invalid/revoked auth; KV hit/miss/unavailable fallback; exact statuses/bodies/CORS/security/cache/rate-limit headers.
- Byte-preserving SSE, abort propagation, `[DONE]`, usage, reservation, settlement, refund, and idempotency checks.
- Redis success/stall/outage parity for the remaining exact organization limiter.
- Trace `entry_dispatch`, `inference_module_init`, rate limits, auth cache/DB, admission/reservation, provider headers, first byte/token, stream completion, and settlement.
- Staging: at least 30 paired warm samples per case, fresh-version cold, and 30-second post-idle samples using the exact-SHA harness.

## Acceptance

- No `bootstrap-app` or 646-route initialization appears in chat traces.
- Cold/post-idle pre-provider p90 improves by at least 50%.
- Warm p50/p90 has no regression beyond measurement noise.
- Zero auth, billing, streaming, CORS/security, or rate-limit semantic differences.
- Rollback through one flag is demonstrated.
